layers.economy_year_control.definition: In Snapshot 2026-10 the year list has 'Latest' and then 2025 down to 2010. 'Latest' shows each dataset's own last year. A chosen year is used by every layer. A dataset with no value for that year shows its latest earlier year, and the layer says '2022 (latest at or before 2023)'. If the year is earlier than the dataset starts, the layer shows its first year and says 'first data 2014'. Snapshot datasets always say 'snapshot 2026'. Play starts at 2010 (or at the chosen year) and moves one year every 1.4 seconds up to the last year (2025), then stops. Choosing a year by hand stops Play. 'Change measured from' lists every year before the last one (2010 to 2024 in Snapshot 2026-10) and starts at 2014. It sets the base of the 'change since the base year' option only. The year and the base are kept in a shared link (ey and eb).
layers.economy_year_control.method: economy.js (ecInitYear, ecResolve, ecChip). The years offered are all years from 2010 on that any yearly dataset holds.
layers.economy_year_control.how_to_read: Check each layer's year chip before comparing two layers. Layers can show different years under one control.
caveats: In Snapshot 2026-10, 'Latest' and '2025' are not the same: survey datasets end in 2024, so choosing 2025 shows their 2024 value with a note.
American Community Survey (ACS) years are five-year windows labeled by their last year, so neighboring years share most of their sample. Compare windows that do not overlap for real change.

On Latest, a pair of layers can come from different years (in Snapshot 2026-10, jobs 2025 and ACS 2024). Check each year chip before you compare two layers, read them as a pair or correlate them. In Snapshot 2026-10 the unemployment rate has no 2020 value, so choosing 2020 shows 2019.

view.label: 2D map: unemployment rate in 2020

layers.workbench.plain: The Workbench is a panel at the bottom of the screen that opens from the Analysis tab. It has ten tabs: Inspector, Table, Scatter, Trend, Correlations, Small multiples, Compare two maps, Composite, Scenarios and Study areas. All of them follow the layers, the year and the settings on the map.
layers.workbench.plain_es: La "Mesa de trabajo" es un panel en la parte inferior de la pantalla que se abre desde la pestaña Análisis. Tiene diez pestañas: "Inspector", "Tabla", "Dispersión", "Tendencia", "Correlaciones", "Mapas pequeños", "Comparar dos mapas", "Índice compuesto", "Escenarios" y "Áreas de estudio". Todas siguen las capas, el año y los ajustes del mapa.
layers.workbench.definition: The 'Workbench' button opens the panel beside the side panel, and the button or the × closes it. The panel's header shows the year, or 'Latest year'. Inspector tab: pick a place from the menu, Puerto Rico as a whole included, or click the map. The table gives each visible layer's value for the place, the Puerto Rico value and a trend line with its length under it (see the entry on trend lines). The other tabs are described in their own entries. It also opens from the link 'Open in the workbench' on a municipality card, from 'View the map as a table' at the foot of the map's legend (the Table tab, so every map can be read as a table) and from buttons in the chat.
layers.workbench.method: economy.js (ecBenchOpen, ecRenderBench, ecBenchInspect; the views of plan item 12: ecBenchMatrix, ecBenchMultiples, ecBenchSwipe, ecBenchComposite; docs/workbench.md).
layers.workbench.how_to_read: Use the Inspector to answer 'what do all my layers say about this place?'.
caveats: A layer that is hidden (eye closed) does not appear in the workbench.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench)

layers.workbench_scatter.plain: The Scatter tab plots one visible layer against another, one dot for each municipality, and gives the correlation between them. It needs two visible layers.
layers.workbench_scatter.plain_es: La pestaña "Dispersión" grafica una capa visible contra otra, con un punto por municipio, y da la correlación entre ambas. Necesita dos capas visibles.
layers.workbench_scatter.definition: Pick the X and Y layers. Each dot is a municipality, and a click on a dot selects it on the map. 'Log scales' draws both axes on a logarithmic scale and keeps only dots where both values are above zero. 'Size by population' scales each dot by the population of the X layer's year. The note above the chart gives the number of municipalities and the correlation coefficient r. A dashed line shows the straight line of best fit (least squares), drawn only when log scales are off. Axis limits are set from the data with a small margin.
layers.workbench_scatter.method: economy.js (ecBenchScatter). r is the Pearson correlation of the plotted values. It is calculated on the values themselves, not on their logarithms, even when log scales are on. The chart is drawn with Chart.js.
layers.workbench_scatter.how_to_read: r runs from −1 to 1. Near 0 means little straight-line relationship. Near ±1 means the dots follow a line closely. The two layers can show different years, so check the chips in the axis titles. With log scales on, the dots look straighter but r still measures the straight-line fit of the raw values, and the fitted line is hidden.
caveats: A correlation across places is not cause and effect. Large places, small samples and survey noise can drive it.
The page says this in the note above the chart.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Scatter)

layers.workbench_table.plain: The Table tab lists the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico with one column for each visible layer. Sort by any column, find a municipality by name and download the table as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
layers.workbench_table.plain_es: La pestaña "Tabla" enumera los 78 municipios y Puerto Rico, con una columna por cada capa visible. Ordene por cualquier columna, busque un municipio por su nombre y descargue la tabla como archivo CSV (valores separados por comas).
layers.workbench_table.definition: Puerto Rico is the first row. Municipalities follow in alphabetical order, in Spanish collation, until you sort by a column. A click on a column title sorts by it, and a second click reverses the order. A box finds municipalities by name. Each column title gives the dataset, its year and, when it is not 'as published', how it is shown. Values are shown rounded as the layer shows them. The button 'Download CSV' saves pr_economy_layers.csv. Its columns are GEOID (the geographic identifier code of the Census Bureau), Municipality and one column for each visible layer, named '<dataset> (<year note>; <show-as code>)'. The file has 79 rows, the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico, in the order of the data file whatever the sort on screen. Values in the file are not rounded for display.
layers.workbench_table.how_to_read: Use the table to look up exact values. Use the CSV to analyze them.
caveats: The CSV holds the values as currently shown, after any 'Show as' option or inflation adjustment. The file does not repeat the margins of error.
Download all years of one dataset, with margins, from its information dialog.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Table)

layers.workbench_trend.plain: The Trend tab draws one line for each chosen place over the years, for one visible layer. Add places, hide lines by clicking their names, and compare each place with Puerto Rico.
layers.workbench_trend.plain_es: La pestaña "Tendencia" dibuja una línea por cada lugar elegido a lo largo de los años, para una capa visible. Agregue lugares, oculte líneas con un clic en sus nombres y compare cada lugar con Puerto Rico.
layers.workbench_trend.definition: Pick a layer (datasets with only one year are not listed) and add places from the menu. The lines follow the layer's settings, such as per 1,000 residents or change since the base year. Years run from 2010 (datasets of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, FEMA, also show earlier years). The Puerto Rico line is thicker. A click on a name in the legend hides or shows that line. 'Reset places' keeps Puerto Rico and the selected municipality. Clicking municipalities on the map adds them. The chart shows up to eight places.
layers.workbench_trend.method: economy.js (ecBenchTrend). Places are kept as a set. The chart draws up to eight of them: Puerto Rico first, then the municipalities in the order of the municipality list. Puerto Rico is never the one left out.
layers.workbench_trend.how_to_read: Compare slopes between places. Check the unit on the vertical axis.
caveats: With more than eight places chosen, the municipalities that come last in the list drop out of the chart without a message. Puerto Rico always stays.

The horizontal axis lists only the years the dataset holds, evenly spaced. In Snapshot 2026-10, a missing year (the unemployment rate has no 2020) or uneven years (FEMA Public Assistance holds 12 declaration years from 2001 to 2024) do not show as gaps, so time can look compressed. The vertical axis is fitted to the data and need not start at zero, so slopes look steeper than the percentage change. A municipality with no value in a listed year is bridged by a straight line.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Trend)

layers.economy_barrio_shading.plain: A shaded layer of the Analysis tab can be drawn on the 901 barrios instead of the 78 municipalities, for the datasets that have values for barrios: the American Community Survey estimates (population, housing, income, age and the others of acs_barrio.json). Datasets published only by municipality, such as jobs and wages, have no barrio values and keep the municipal map.
layers.economy_barrio_shading.plain_es: Una capa sombreada de la pestaña Análisis puede dibujarse sobre los 901 barrios en vez de los 78 municipios, para los conjuntos de datos que tienen valores por barrio: los estimados de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad (población, vivienda, ingreso, edad y los demás de acs_barrio.json). Los datos que solo se publican por municipio, como los empleos y los salarios, no tienen valores por barrio y mantienen el mapa municipal.
layers.economy_barrio_shading.definition: In the Analysis tab, Settings of a shaded layer, Area: Municipalities or Barrios. The choice is offered when the dataset is in acs_barrio.json (the data dictionary lists the barrio level for it) and the layer is the only shaded one; symbols and two shaded layers together stay municipal. The barrio values are the American Community Survey 5-year estimates for the 901 Census county subdivisions, with their margins of error: a barrio whose margin is above 30% of its estimate is hatched, as on the municipal map. A value is shown as published or as a percentile among the barrios; the rescalings that need a municipio's residents or land (per 1,000 residents, per km², share of Puerto Rico) fall back to the published value, and the legend says so. Hovering a barrio shows its name, municipality, value and margin of error. The link keeps the choice (mode code b). The workbench views, the table and the click pop-ups stay municipal.
layers.economy_barrio_shading.method: js/econ_level.js, loaded the first time a layer asks for it, reads the engine's contract for the layer at the barrio level (E.series with level 'barrio', from acs_barrio.json via economy.js ecLoadLevel), cuts five classes from the barrio values with the layer's own method (quantiles, equal intervals, natural breaks or own limits) and colors barrios.geojson by them.
layers.economy_barrio_shading.how_to_read: Small areas have wide margins: in the 2020-2024 window, 387 of the 901 barrios have a less reliable median household income and 112 have none. Read the hatching before comparing two barrios, and use the CSV by area for the exact margins.
caveats: Only datasets with barrio values in the files: municipal-only datasets are not split among barrios, because no source gives their barrio values and the observatory does not estimate them.
Barrios are Census county subdivisions; their boundaries are those of 2020.
layers.economy_barrio_shading.source_detail: acs_barrio.json (American Community Survey 5-year estimates for county subdivisions); barrios.geojson (Census TIGERweb county subdivisions).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: a shaded layer, Settings, Area

layers.trend_sparkline.plain: A small gray line with a blue dot shows how a value changed over the years for one municipality. The label under it says how many years the line covers, for example '12 yrs'.
layers.trend_sparkline.plain_es: Una pequeña línea gris con un punto azul muestra cómo cambió un valor a lo largo de los años en un municipio. La etiqueta debajo indica cuántos años abarca la línea, por ejemplo "12 años".
layers.trend_sparkline.definition: The blue dot marks the year on screen. The label under the line gives the length of the trend: 'N yrs' ('yrs' means years) is the number of calendar years from the first to the last year drawn, both included. If some years have no value, the label adds how many values were drawn, for example '12 yrs, 9 values'. On the Analysis tab the label also gives the first and last year, for example '12 yrs · 2014–25'. The column header of the lines in the workbench's Inspector tab (the map popup has no trend lines) reads 'Trend', with the note 'years shown; dot = chosen year'. The label itself starts with the number of years. The Housing profile has no header. A line needs at least two yearly values, so datasets with one year have none. The line scales from the lowest to the highest value drawn, so a flat-looking line can hold a large change. Economy lines start in 2010 at the earliest. Housing profile lines use every year the dataset has.
layers.trend_sparkline.method: economy.js (ecSpark) and housing.js (spark) draw the same small chart. The label is calculated from the years of the values drawn.
layers.trend_sparkline.how_to_read: Compare the shape and the length, not the height. Two lines of different datasets are each drawn to fill the same small space.
caveats: Survey series (American Community Survey, ACS) use overlapping five-year windows, so their lines are smoother than the real change.
A series with a break, such as the population series that steps up in 2020, shows the break as a jump.
For survey series the length counts window labels. Each label is a five-year window, so the line covers more time than the label says.
The Economy line follows the layer's 'Show as' and inflation settings. The Housing line shows values as published.
layers.trend_sparkline.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json (the series drawn). The small chart carries no credit line.

view.label: Housing page: municipality profile with trend lines

layers.workbench_swipe.plain: Two layers on one map of Puerto Rico with a divider you can drag: the left side shows one layer and the right side the other.
layers.workbench_swipe.plain_es: Dos capas en un mismo mapa de Puerto Rico con una división que se puede arrastrar: el lado izquierdo muestra una capa y el derecho la otra.
layers.workbench_swipe.definition: Pick the left and the right layer among the visible layers. The slider moves the divider across the island; each side keeps its own classes and has its own legend below the map. Hovering a municipality gives both values. The slider works with the keyboard (arrow keys).
layers.workbench_swipe.method: economy.js (ecBenchSwipe): one SVG with the second layer clipped at the divider.
layers.workbench_swipe.how_to_read: Move the divider slowly over a region to see whether the two layers are high in the same places.
caveats: The two sides have different classes: a dark color on each side means high for that layer, not the same number.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Compare two maps)

layers.workbench_matrix.plain: A table of the correlation between every pair of visible layers, so you can see at a glance which ones move together across the municipalities.
layers.workbench_matrix.plain_es: Una tabla con la correlación entre cada par de capas visibles, para ver de un vistazo cuáles se mueven juntas entre los municipios.
layers.workbench_matrix.definition: Up to eight visible layers, each as it is on the map (its year, rescaling and settings). Each cell gives r and n, the number of municipalities that have a value for both layers of the pair; each pair uses its own municipalities (pairwise complete), so n can differ between cells. Pearson measures a straight-line pattern; Spearman (rank order) measures whether the ranks rise or fall together, which a few very large values do not dominate. A pair with fewer than 3 municipalities gets no r. Colors: dark red below −0.5, light red −0.5 to −0.1, gray −0.1 to 0.1, light blue 0.1 to 0.5, dark blue above 0.5.
layers.workbench_matrix.method: economy.js (ecBenchMatrix) with Core.stats.matrix and Core.stats.correlation (site/js/core/stats.js; Spearman is Pearson on the ranks, ties sharing the mean of their ranks).
layers.workbench_matrix.how_to_read: Read a cell as a pattern across places: a dark blue cell means municipalities with more of one tend to have more of the other. Check n before comparing two cells.
caveats: A correlation across places is not cause and effect, and it does not describe the people inside a place.
Large places, survey noise and a third factor can drive a correlation.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Correlations)

layers.scenarios.plain: Save what the map shows as a scenario, compare two scenarios figure by figure, and load the results of an outside model as a layer marked as model output, not observed data.
layers.scenarios.plain_es: Guarde lo que muestra el mapa como un escenario, compare dos escenarios cifra por cifra y cargue los resultados de un modelo externo como una capa marcada como resultado de modelo, no datos observados.
layers.scenarios.definition: A scenario keeps the map's link (layers, year, composite, planned route), the figures it produced (the planned route's measures and Puerto Rico's value of each visible layer, with its year and settings) and any model output loaded with it. Scenarios stay in the browser (IndexedDB); 'Export' saves one as a JSON file and 'Import a scenario' reads it back after checking it. 'Open scenario' restores the view, and its model outputs, from the link. 'Compare two scenarios' lists every figure with A, B, B − A and the change in percent; when both scenarios hold a model output of the same variable, 'Map B − A' shades the difference. Names, labels and notes refuse e-mail addresses and telephone numbers: a scenario names a team or organization, not a person's contact.
layers.scenarios.method: js/scenarios.js (loaded the first time the tab opens) and Core.scenario (site/js/core/scenario.js: make, check, read, diff, parseModel, diffSeries); economy.js (ecBenchScenarios, ecScenarioLib). The link part sc= reopens a scenario that holds model outputs.
layers.scenarios.how_to_read: A difference between two scenarios is the difference between two views or two model runs, not a forecast.
caveats: Scenarios live in this browser only: clearing the browser's data deletes them. Export the ones to keep.
A figure saved with one year or setting is another figure from the same dataset with another year or setting.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Scenarios)

layers.workbench_multiples.plain: Many small maps side by side: one map for each year of a layer, or one map for each visible layer, so changes and differences show at a glance.
layers.workbench_multiples.plain_es: Muchos mapas pequeños uno al lado del otro: un mapa por cada año de una capa, o un mapa por cada capa visible, para ver cambios y diferencias de un vistazo.
layers.workbench_multiples.definition: 'One map for each year of one layer' draws the chosen layer in each of its last 12 years that have values, with one set of classes for every map (worked out from all the years together), so a color means the same in each year; the Puerto Rico value is under each map. 'One map for each visible layer' draws up to eight visible layers at the year each shows, each with its own classes, so colors are not comparable between maps. Hover a municipality for its value. The maps have no base map.
layers.workbench_multiples.method: economy.js (ecBenchMultiples, ecClassFill) with Core.minimap (site/js/core/minimap.js), which draws the 78 municipal outlines as SVG.
layers.workbench_multiples.how_to_read: In the maps by year, a municipality that darkens from map to map is rising against the same classes.
caveats: In the maps by layer each map has its own classes: compare where values are high or low, not the colors.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Small multiples)

layers.study_areas.plain: Load your own polygons, such as a neighborhood or a service area, and see what each holds: residents, transit stops and, on request, tourism places and flood and protected land, plus every dataset of the Analysis tab estimated for each area.
layers.study_areas.plain_es: Cargue sus propios polígonos, como un vecindario o un área de servicio, y vea qué contiene cada uno: residentes, paradas de transporte y, si lo pide, lugares turísticos y terreno inundable o protegido, además de cada conjunto de datos de la pestaña Análisis estimado para cada área.
layers.study_areas.definition: A GeoJSON file of polygons in longitude and latitude, up to 200 areas, is read in the browser and never uploaded; only each area's name and shape are kept, with the set's name, source and description, in IndexedDB. For each area: its km², residents by Census 2020 block centroid, residents more than 800 m from a scheduled stop, scheduled transit stops and, on request, tourism places and the share of its land in a FEMA flood hazard area (zones A and V) and in a protected area. Every dataset of the Analysis tab is estimated for each area from the municipios it covers: totals by the share of each municipio's residents inside (land, for totals measured in km²), an exact sum when the area holds whole municipios; rates and levels as an average weighted by the residents inside. Each row names its method.
layers.study_areas.method: js/studyareas.js (loaded the first time the tab opens) and Core.study (site/js/core/study.js: parse, make, check, read, toGeoJSON, measure, estimate); economy.js (ecBenchStudy, ecStudyLib). docs/study-areas.md.
layers.study_areas.how_to_read: The estimates assume a municipio is the same throughout: a small area inside one municipio gets that municipio's rate. Counted measures (residents, stops, places) are counts inside the area; the dataset rows are estimates.
caveats: Study areas live in this browser only: clearing the browser's data deletes them. Export the ones to keep.
Survey margins of error are not carried into the estimates.
Residents are placed at the center of their census block, so a block cut by an edge counts wholly on the side of its center.
layers.study_areas.geography: Polygons the user loads, within Puerto Rico

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Study areas)

layers.walk_rings.plain: 'Show 400 m walk radius around stops' draws a circle of 400 meters around each stop, bus station, Tren Urbano station and ferry terminal. The circles appear only when you are zoomed in and the stops or stations layer is on.
layers.walk_rings.plain_es: "Mostrar radio de 400 m a pie alrededor de las paradas" dibuja un círculo de 400 metros alrededor de cada parada, estación de guaguas, estación del Tren Urbano y terminal de lanchas. Los círculos solo aparecen al acercar el mapa y cuando la capa de paradas o la de estaciones está activada.
layers.walk_rings.definition: 400 meters is about a quarter mile, a common planning distance for walking to a stop. It is a choice made for the observatory, not a measure of how far people walk. The rings are thin blue circles with a very light blue fill and a 400 m radius, drawn in Snapshot 2026-10 for 4,360 points (the 4,240 stops and the 120 stations and terminals, airports excluded). They show when the switch is on, the map zoom is 14 or higher, and 'Transit stops' or 'Stations, terminals & airports' is on. If only one of those two layers is on, the rings of both kinds still appear. Rings overlap where stops are close. The same distance defines 'within 400 m of any mapped stop' and 'within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable' in the statistics. The 3D view has the same switch, under the same conditions: the rings lie flat on the ground with a radius of 400 meters at every zoom (a MapLibre circle whose radius in pixels doubles at each zoom level, set from each point's latitude), and the chip counts them while they are drawn.
layers.walk_rings.method: app.js (updateRings): ringLayer holds one circle for each point of kind transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station and ferry_terminal. twin3d.js (addRings, updateRings) draws the same points in the 3D view.
layers.walk_rings.how_to_read: Look at what the circles cover and what they leave out. Places outside every circle are more than 400 m, in a straight line, from the nearest stop.
caveats: The distance is a straight line. It ignores rivers, hills, fences and the street pattern.
Rings include stops of expired timetables and OpenStreetMap stops that have no timetable.
The rings say nothing about how often or when a vehicle comes.

A place inside a ring can still have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m: the ring may belong to a stop whose timetable has ended or to a volunteer-mapped stop. The place's pop-up gives its access class.
layers.walk_rings.source_detail: transport.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 4,360 points of kind transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station and ferry_terminal. The stops come from timetable feeds of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and of municipalities in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form, and from OpenStreetMap. The rings carry no credit line of their own. The stops or stations layer that must be on shows its own credit line: see the entries on those two layers.

view.label: 2D map: 400 m rings at Santurce, San Juan
3D view: switch on Transit stops and the 400 m rings (Santurce, San Juan)

layers.barrios_control.plain: The 'Barrios' switch draws the 901 barrios of the Census Bureau's January 2023 layer, the districts inside each municipality, as dashed outlines. Click inside one for its counts.
layers.barrios_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Barrios" dibuja con líneas discontinuas los 901 barrios de la capa de enero de 2023 del Negociado del Censo, que son las divisiones dentro de cada municipio. Haga clic dentro de uno para ver sus conteos.
layers.barrios_control.definition: Barrios are dashed blue outlines. The layer is off when the page opens. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads barrios.geojson (about 1.0 MB in Snapshot 2026-10). With the switch on, a click adds a section to the popup. It gives the barrio's name, its municipality and its area in square kilometers. It also gives the number of tourism places, the places per square kilometer, how many of those places are in a flood hazard area, and how many are within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (and how many of those are near a frequent stop) and within 400 m of any mapped stop. The 3D view has the same switch: the same dashed outlines and, for a click inside a barrio, the same section, last in the card after the other areas under the click, as on the 2D map.
layers.barrios_control.method: app.js (loadBarrios), twin3d.js (addBarrios) and access.js (barrioPopup, shared by both views). The counts are stored in barrios.geojson.
layers.barrios_control.how_to_read: Compare barrios by places per square kilometer, not by raw counts, because their areas differ a great deal.
caveats: A barrio is a Census statistical unit. It is not a neighborhood or an electoral unit.
Barrio names repeat across municipalities. Read the municipality in the popup.

Barrio counts use the default filters (confidence 0.50, no places of worship). The confidence slider, the category buttons and the worship switch do not change them. The counts are rebuilt only at a full build, so between full builds they can lag the municipality figures.
Cite the outlines as the Census Bureau's generalized county-subdivision boundaries as of January 1, 2023, cut at the shoreline.
layers.barrios_control.source_detail: barrios.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Barrios: US Census Bureau'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Barrios (Bayamón area)
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Barrios (Bayamón area)

layers.place_categories.plain: Four buttons under the Tourism places switch turn each tourism category on or off: Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations and Visitor Services. All four are on when the page opens.
layers.place_categories.plain_es: Cuatro botones bajo el interruptor "Lugares turísticos" activan o desactivan cada categoría turística: "Atracciones", "Gastronomía", "Alojamientos" y "Servicios para visitantes". Las cuatro están activadas al abrir la página.
layers.place_categories.definition: Each button shows or hides every place of one category. A pressed button is on. A button that is off looks faded. The buttons change the pins, the live tiles and tables of the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places file in comma-separated values (CSV) form. The 3D view has the same four buttons. The statistics of each municipality (Rankings tab, shading) do not follow the buttons. Pin and button colors: Attractions blue, Gastronomy green, Accommodations gold, Visitor Services red.
layers.place_categories.method: app.js (renderCatChips) keeps a set of the categories that are on and rebuilds the pins when a button is pressed. Colors and icons are defined once in icons.js. Pressing a button sets aria-pressed for screen readers.
layers.place_categories.how_to_read: A category is a group of Overture categories that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) assigned. See the entry on classification for how the groups were made.
caveats: Places of Worship belong to Attractions, so they show only when the Attractions button and the worship switch are both on.
Color is not the only cue. The pin icon and the type in the card also say what a place is.

values.ATTRACTIONS: Attractions, blue (#338CB3). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Beaches, Historic Sites, Nature Reserves, Scenic Areas, Parks, Tourist Attractions, Places of Worship, Cultural Attractions, Museums.
values.GASTRONOMY: Gastronomy, green (#79901E). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Restaurants, Bars, Cafes, Bakeries, Nightlife, Food Experiences.
values.ACCOMMODATIONS: Accommodations, gold (#FFA600). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Hotels, Lodging, Vacation Properties, Guest Houses, Resorts, Inns.
values.VISITOR_SERVICES: Visitor Services, red (#FF4D38). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Transportation, Marinas, Tour Operators, Visitor Centers, Adventure Operators, Cultural Experience Providers.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: category buttons

layers.click_popup.plain: A click on the 2D map opens a popup for the overlays that are on at that spot. If no overlay has anything there, a click on a municipality opens its profile.
layers.click_popup.plain_es: Un clic en el mapa 2D abre una ventana emergente con las capas superpuestas que están activadas en ese lugar. Si ninguna tiene datos ahí, un clic en un municipio abre su perfil.
layers.click_popup.definition: In this order, the popup can hold: up to two flood zones, up to two protected areas, the land-use class of one polygon (water and road polygons are skipped), and one barrio. If the boundaries layer is on and the click is inside a municipality, a link 'Open the <name> profile' is added. If no overlay has a feature at the point, the click selects the municipality (when Boundaries is on) and opens the Municipality tab. Pins, stops, routes and vehicle dots have their own popups. Two modes take the click away: choosing a point for the route planner, and having the Analysis tab open with at least one visible layer. In the second case the click opens the economy popup for the municipality.
layers.click_popup.method: app.js (the map click handler) with featuresAt in plan.js. Overlays are not interactive, so a polygon layer cannot swallow clicks meant for the municipality below it.
layers.click_popup.how_to_read: Switch on the overlays you want to read before you click.
caveats: The popup shows up to two flood zones and two protected areas. A point with more overlapping records shows only the first ones.

view.label: 2D map

layers.flood_zones_control.plain: The 'Flood zones' switch shades the land that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as flood-prone, from its National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL). It is off when the page opens. With it on, a click on the map tells you the FEMA zone at that point.
layers.flood_zones_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Zonas inundables" sombrea los terrenos que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) identifica como propensos a inundarse en su NFHL (Capa Nacional de Riesgo de Inundación). Está desactivado al abrir la página. Con el interruptor activado, un clic en el mapa muestra la zona de FEMA en ese punto.
layers.flood_zones_control.definition: The legend on the Map layers tab has four rows. Darkest blue is for V and VE zones (coastal high hazard, wave action). Mid blue is for A, AE, AH, AO and A99 zones (1% annual chance, the Special Flood Hazard Area). Red is for the regulatory floodway. Light blue is for the shaded X zone (0.2% annual chance). The first time you switch it on, the page downloads flood.geojson (about 8 MB in Snapshot 2026-10). With the switch on, a click adds a section 'Flood zone' to the popup, for up to two zones under the click, with a plain description (1% annual chance, 0.2% annual chance, or 'see FEMA zone definitions') and the zone subtype. The layer itself does not take clicks, so the municipality underneath still answers.
layers.flood_zones_control.method: app.js (floodStyle, floodVisible, loadFlood, floodPopup). The 2D map draws a polygon when FEMA labels it as in the Special Flood Hazard Area or as the shaded 0.2% X zone. Minimal-hazard X, zone D and the labels OPEN WATER and AREA NOT INCLUDED are not drawn. Click answers use point-in-polygon tests on the same file (plan.js, featuresAt).
layers.flood_zones_control.how_to_read: Read the color as the FEMA zone family, not as depth. An unshaded area is not proof of safety.
caveats: This is FEMA's mapped hazard at a location. It is not a forecast for any year and it says nothing about a building's elevation or insurance.
Drawn outlines are simplified. See the flood layer entry for the effect at zone edges.
If the file cannot be downloaded, the switch turns itself off.

This is a simplified copy of FEMA's data for context. FEMA's printed flood maps and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. It is not a flood determination for any property. Read the source's terms before you rely on it.
layers.flood_zones_control.source_detail: flood.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Flood zones: FEMA NFHL'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Hazards and environment, Flood zones (FEMA)

layers.worship_toggle.plain: 'Include places of worship' adds churches and other places of worship to the pins. It is off when the page opens, because most of them are not tourism supply.
layers.worship_toggle.plain_es: "Incluir lugares de culto" agrega iglesias y otros lugares de culto a los marcadores. Está desactivado al abrir la página, porque la mayoría no forma parte de la oferta turística.
layers.worship_toggle.definition: Places of worship are the listings of type 'Places of Worship', which belong to the Attractions category. The places file of Snapshot 2026-10 holds 5,032 of them, and 4,758 have a confidence score of 0.50 or more. With the switch off, none is drawn or counted. With it on, those that pass the other filters appear. Only the 2D map has this switch. The 3D view, the route planner, the municipality statistics and the Rankings tab always leave places of worship out.
layers.worship_toggle.method: app.js: a place is visible when the switch is on or its type is not 'Places of Worship'. The page's help text calls these places landmarks and heritage assets.
layers.worship_toggle.how_to_read: Turn the switch on to see landmarks such as churches on the map. Do not read them as visitor attractions in the statistics, because the statistics leave them out.
caveats: The listing does not say whether a place of worship is open to visitors.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Include places of worship

layers.landuse_analysis.plain: A panel that shows how the land of Puerto Rico and of each municipality divides among the classes of the 2015 land use plan, as bars and tables, with all 78 municipalities side by side. It opens from the Land use group of the Map layers tab.
layers.landuse_analysis.plain_es: Un panel que muestra cómo se reparte el terreno de Puerto Rico y de cada municipio entre las clases del plan de uso de terrenos de 2015, con barras y tablas, y los 78 municipios uno al lado del otro. Se abre desde el grupo Uso de terrenos de la pestaña Capas del mapa.
layers.landuse_analysis.definition: The button 'Land use by municipality and for Puerto Rico', in the Land use group of the Map layers tab, opens a panel under the map (it replaces the Economy workbench while open). It shows the chosen area (Puerto Rico or a municipality) as one bar split by class, with the km² and the share of land of each, and the 78 municipalities as bars sorted by the share of a class you choose. It can show the ten classes of the legend or the four groups (urban, for urban growth, ordinary rural, specially protected rural). Clicking a municipality shows it and moves the map there. The CSV holds the km² and shares of every area.
layers.landuse_analysis.method: js/landuse_view.js reads landuse_summary.json and divides each class (or group) by the land of the area in the plan: the sum of the classes with in_share, so water and road rights-of-way are left out. Nothing is computed from the map's simplified polygons.
layers.landuse_analysis.how_to_read: Each bar is 100% of the land in the plan of that area; water and road rights-of-way are left out. Hover a segment for its class and share. The table under the chosen area gives the exact figures.
caveats: A planning classification, not land cover.
The analysis always shows every class: unticking a class in the legend hides it on the map only.
layers.landuse_analysis.source_detail: landuse_summary.json (landuse.py class_summary); the script js/landuse_view.js loads the first time the panel opens.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab, Land use: Land use by municipality and for Puerto Rico

layers.confidence_filter.plain: The 'Minimum confidence' slider hides tourism places that Overture rates below the chosen score. It starts at 0.50. Lower it to see more listings, or raise it to see fewer.
layers.confidence_filter.plain_es: El control deslizante "Confianza mínima" oculta los lugares turísticos a los que Overture da una puntuación menor que la elegida. Empieza en 0.50. Bájelo para ver más listados, o súbalo para ver menos.
layers.confidence_filter.definition: Overture gives each listing a confidence score from 0 to 1, its estimate that the listing is a real, current place. The slider runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05. The number beside it changes as you move the slider, and the map redraws when you let go. In Snapshot 2026-10 the scores run from 0.024 to 1.0. At 0.50 the map shows 24,209 places. At 0 it shows 27,509. Places of worship are left out of both counts. The slider also sets the live numbers on the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places file in comma-separated values (CSV) form.
layers.confidence_filter.method: app.js keeps the value in S.conf. A place is visible when its confidence is at or above it, its category button is on and it is not a place of worship (unless the worship switch is on).
layers.confidence_filter.how_to_read: 0.50 is the observatory's own cut-off, not an Overture rule. In Snapshot 2026-10 it keeps 24,209 of the 27,509 listings (88%) that are not places of worship. A score is Overture's estimate, and a high score does not prove that a place is open today.
caveats: Only the 2D map has this slider. The 3D view, the route planner and the municipality statistics always use 0.50.
The slider does not change the numbers on the Rankings tab or in the shading. Those use the stored statistics.

The note under the slider on the page says 0.50 keeps 'the reliable majority'. The observatory has no test of reliability. 0.50 is a chosen cut-off, and the listings below it are not shown to be wrong.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Minimum confidence

layers.boundaries_control.plain: The 'Municipal boundaries' switch draws the outlines of the 78 municipalities. It is on when the page opens. Pointing at a municipality shows a short summary, and a click opens its profile.
layers.boundaries_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Límites municipales" dibuja los contornos de los 78 municipios. Está activado al abrir la página. Al pasar el cursor sobre un municipio aparece un resumen breve, y un clic abre su perfil.
layers.boundaries_control.definition: Outlines are blue lines. Names appear from zoom level 10. Pointing at a municipality (with a mouse) thickens its outline and shows a box with its name, its number of tourism places, the share of those places in a flood hazard area and its 2020 population. A click opens the Municipality tab and outlines the municipality in red. When a flood, protected-area, land-use or barrio layer is on and has a feature under the click, the popup comes first, with a link 'Open the <name> profile'. When the switch is off, a click no longer selects a municipality and the outlines and names disappear. The 3D view has the same switch, on when it opens and never counted, as on the 2D map: it shows or hides the outlines only (no labels, no hover box), and a click on a municipality opens its card with the outlines on or off. When a flood zone, protected area, land-use class, Comunidad Especial or barrio is under the click, the card of those areas comes first, with the same link 'Open the <name> profile', which opens the municipality's card.
layers.boundaries_control.method: app.js (init, muniStyle, selectMuni). In the 3D view, twin3d.js draws the outlines (muni-line) and the switch lyMuni shows or hides them.
layers.boundaries_control.how_to_read: Use the outline to see which municipality a place is in. The summary box counts places with the default filters.
caveats: Outlines are generalized shoreline-clipped shapes. Do not use them to decide whether a lot lies inside a municipality.
Cite the outlines as the Census Bureau's generalized boundaries as of January 1, 2023, cut at the shoreline. Only the population is a 2020 count.
layers.boundaries_control.source_detail: municipios.geojson and municipalities.json. Credit line on the map: 'Boundaries & population: US Census 2020'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Boundaries
3D view, Layers tab: Territory, Municipal boundaries

layers.landuse_control.plain: The 'Land use 2015' switch shades the whole island by the Junta de Planificación's land-use plan: urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural and specially protected rural land. It is off when the page opens.
layers.landuse_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Uso de terrenos 2015" sombrea toda la isla según el plan de uso de terrenos de la Junta de Planificación (JP): suelo urbano, urbanizable, rústico común y rústico especialmente protegido. Está desactivado al abrir la página.
layers.landuse_control.definition: The legend has ten rows with their colors. Suelo Urbano (urban) is gray. Urbanizable programado (planned growth) is orange. Urbanizable no programado (reserve growth) is light gold. Rústico común (ordinary rural) is light green. Rústico especialmente protegido (protected rural) is green. The five special protection classes (ecological, agricultural, hydric, ecological and hydric, agricultural and hydric) are dark green, lime and blues. Other protection combinations in the data use the color stored in the file. Water and road polygons are not drawn. Polygons are drawn at 50% opacity. A click adds a section to the popup with the class name, the class code and the municipio of the first polygon under the click. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads landuse.geojson (about 17.7 MB in Snapshot 2026-10), the largest file of the map. A note under the legend says that zoning districts (Calificación) are not shown, because the Junta's service did not answer when Snapshot 2026-10 was built. Since 2026-10-16 every class of the legend has a tick box, ticked when the layer opens: unticking a class hides it on the map and in the click pop-up. The button above the legend opens the land-use analysis (layers.landuse_analysis).
layers.landuse_control.method: app.js (loadLanduse, landusePopup). The layer filters out the groups water and road. Colors are stored in the file.
layers.landuse_control.how_to_read: Use it for the broad pattern of where the plan allows growth and where it protects land.
caveats: The plan is a classification for planning. It is not a zoning map and does not say what may be built on a lot.
The plan dates from 2015. Land may since have been built on, reclassified or protected.
Polygons are simplified, so do not use the layer to decide the class of one lot.
layers.landuse_control.source_detail: landuse.geojson. File version label: 'PUT-2014, 30-NOV-2015', the plan of 30 November 2015, which the page calls Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015. Credit line on the map: 'Land use: Junta de Planificación'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015

layers.protected_control.plain: The 'Protected areas' switch shades the protected areas of the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) of the US Geological Survey (USGS), from national forests to local parks. It holds 665 records in Snapshot 2026-10. Records overlap, so this is not a count of separate areas. The switch is off when the page opens.
layers.protected_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Áreas protegidas" sombrea las áreas protegidas de PAD-US (Base de Datos de Áreas Protegidas de Estados Unidos), del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos), desde bosques nacionales hasta parques locales. Tiene 665 registros en el corte de datos de 2026-10. Los registros se superponen, así que no es un conteo de áreas separadas. El interruptor está desactivado al abrir la página.
layers.protected_control.definition: Areas are drawn in green at 30% opacity. With the switch on, a click adds a section to the popup for up to two protected areas under the click. It gives the name, the designation (in Snapshot 2026-10 the data hold 22 codes: the card spells out 10 of them, for example National Forest or Local Park, and shows the raw code for the other 12, such as SCA, SRMA and MIL, which covers 126 of the 665 records), the manager, the public access (open access, restricted access, closed or unknown), the acres and the Gap Analysis Project (GAP) status. The GAP status is a rating from 1 to 4 of how strictly the land is managed for nature. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads protected.geojson (about 1.5 MB in Snapshot 2026-10).
layers.protected_control.method: app.js (protStyle, protPopup, padTxt, loadProt). The codes are spelled out with the lists in the PAD constant, taken from the PAD-US data dictionary.
layers.protected_control.how_to_read: Check the designation and the GAP status before you read a patch as a nature reserve.
caveats: 'Protected' has a wide meaning here. It includes recreation areas, local parks and military land.
Overlapping areas are stacked, so a darker patch can be several records.

In Snapshot 2026-10 the card spells out the designation for 539 of the 665 records. For the other 126 records (codes such as SCA, SRMA and MIL) it shows the raw PAD-US code. Look the code up in the entry on the designation. A military area, for example, shows only 'MIL'.

In Snapshot 2026-10 two thirds of the records (440 of 665) have GAP status 4, which the card words as 'no known biodiversity mandate'. Read the GAP status before you treat a patch as a nature reserve.
layers.protected_control.source_detail: protected.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Protected areas: USGS PAD-US'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Protected areas

municipalities.quintile_shading.plain: The map ranks the 78 municipalities on the chosen statistic and splits them into five groups of about the same size. It shades the groups from light blue (lowest) to dark blue (highest).
municipalities.quintile_shading.plain_es: El mapa ordena los 78 municipios según la estadística escogida y los divide en cinco grupos de tamaño parecido. Colorea los grupos de azul claro (el más bajo) a azul oscuro (el más alto).
municipalities.quintile_shading.definition: The municipalities that have a value are sorted from lowest to highest. The class limits are the values found one fifth, two fifths, three fifths and four fifths of the way along the sorted list. On the 2D map a municipality takes the first class whose upper limit is at or above its value. With 78 municipalities each class holds about 15 or 16, fewer or more when several municipalities share a value. The five blues run from light (lowest) to dark (highest). Municipalities with no value are not shaded.
municipalities.quintile_shading.method: Functions breaks and setChoro in site/js/app.js. The legend lists the range and the number of municipalities in each class. The 3D view colors its columns with the same four class limits and sets each column's height in proportion to the value, with the largest value tallest. Population change 2010 to 2020 is drawn as a one-sided scale in the 3D view because all 78 municipalities lost population: taller and redder columns mean bigger losses. The 2D map shades any dataset this way from Explore, the Catalog or Rankings (the 'Shade municipalities by' menu with its 25 options was retired on 2026-11-05); the 3D menu of Columns by municipality has 17 (see '3D view: Columns by municipality').
municipalities.quintile_shading.how_to_read: Read the legend, because the same color means different numbers for each statistic. Darker means a higher value than most other municipalities, not a good or bad result. Some fields of the municipality table cannot be shaded, such as land area, the housing unit counts, the 2010 population, places by category, the average confidence, the shares of places within 800 m of a stop with a current timetable or within 400 m of a rail station or ferry terminal, and the stop counts by timetable state. Population change 2010 to 2020 is shaded in the 3D view only. Places inside protected areas and places with a website are offered on the Rankings tab, not in the shading menu.
caveats: The groups have equal size, not equal width. A municipality at the top of one class can have almost the same value as one at the bottom of the next.

The 3D view uses the same four limits, but a municipality whose value equals a limit takes the lower class on the 2D map and the higher class in the 3D view. Its color can therefore differ by one step between the two views.

The legend and the Rankings tab round values: whole numbers for counts and most percentages; one decimal for places per 1,000 residents, places per km² and the seasonal share; two decimals for the affordability ratio. The stored values can have more decimals (two for places per 1,000 residents and per km², one for the share in a flood hazard area). Cite the stored value from the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
Shading shows rank among the 78 municipalities, not distance from any target.
municipalities.quintile_shading.source_detail: Inputs are the municipalities.* fields named in the method; the classes are a display choice of the observatory.

view.label: Map, a dataset shaded in five classes (an old 'Shade municipalities by' link)
3D view: 'Columns by municipality'

layers.region_filter.plain: The 'Region' filter of the Reference group outlines a region's municipios, fades the rest of the island and frames the map on it, in the 2D map and the 3D view. The data layers are not cut.
layers.region_filter.plain_es: El filtro "Región" del grupo Referencia delinea los municipios de una región, atenúa el resto de la isla y encuadra el mapa en ella, en el mapa 2D y en la vista 3D. Las capas de datos no se recortan.
layers.region_filter.definition: The menu lists 'All of Puerto Rico', then the FPR planning regions (the Eastern Region of the Eastern Region Strategic Vision, ERSV, 15 municipios) and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company's seven tourism regions, each with its number of municipios. They are the regions of geo/regions.json, the same list as the 2D map's Region tab and the regional profile. Picking one draws a dark outline around each of its municipios, lays a white veil (55% opacity) over the other municipios and frames the map on the region (in 3D the camera tilts to at least 45 degrees). The veil sits above the data layers and under the markers and pop-ups, and nothing in it takes a click, so every layer still answers a click everywhere. The note under the menu says how many municipios are outlined and links to the regional profile. 'All of Puerto Rico' takes the outline and the veil away. The pick is kept in the address as rg=<id> and travels in the links between the 2D map and the 3D view.
layers.region_filter.method: core/regionfilter.js (split, leaflet, maplibre, control), loaded by app.js and twin3d.js on use (the first time the Reference group opens, or at ready when the address has rg=), with geo/regions.json. The address key rg= is read and written by core/viewstate.js. HANDOFF decision 113.
layers.region_filter.how_to_read: Use it to look at one region with any layer on: the region stands out, and the faded rest of the island gives context. For a region's own figures, open the Region tab or the regional profile.
caveats: The filter frames the map; it does not filter the data. Legends, counts, rankings, the Explore panel and every download still cover all of Puerto Rico.
Markers (the tourism places' pins and clusters) are drawn above the veil, so they are not faded outside the region.
layers.region_filter.geography: 8 regions, each a set of whole municipios

view.label: 2D map, Layers tab: Reference, Region (Eastern Region)
3D view, Layers tab: Reference, Region (Eastern Region)

layers.slr_control.plain: The 'Sea level rise' switch shows a map from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) of land that would be flooded at the highest regular high tides if the sea rose by 1 to 10 feet. The slider picks the number of feet, and it starts at 3.
layers.slr_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Aumento del nivel del mar" muestra un mapa de NOAA (Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica) con los terrenos que se inundarían en la marea alta más alta de cada día si el mar subiera de 1 a 10 pies. El control deslizante elige la cantidad de pies y empieza en 3.
layers.slr_control.definition: The layer is off when the page opens. The slider runs from 1 to 10 feet in steps of 1. The label beside it says the chosen height, for example '3 ft'. When the layer is on, NOAA's tiles are drawn at 65% opacity. Moving the slider swaps the layer when you let go. The page address keeps the choice as slr=N. If NOAA does not answer, a message appears. The tiles are enlarged beyond zoom level 16. The page keeps no copy of the sea level data.
layers.slr_control.method: app.js (setSlr, slrUrl) asks https://coast.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/dc_slr/slr_{N}ft/MapServer for tiles, where N is the slider value.
layers.slr_control.how_to_read: Read it as a what-if for planning: 'land that would be wet at this height'. It is not a timeline and it names no year.
caveats: The page calls this a what-if for planning, not a timeline. NOAA says the layer shows water at the highest high tides and does not model storm surge, erosion, subsidence or new construction. NOAA calls it a planning reference that should not be used for navigation, permitting or other legal purposes.
If NOAA changes or removes the service, the layer stops working. The observatory cannot restore it.
layers.slr_control.source_detail: NOAA Office for Coastal Management, Sea Level Rise Viewer. Credit line on the map: 'Sea level rise: NOAA OCM'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Sea level rise, 5 ft

layers.shade_by.plain: A menu of the 2D map that colored the 78 municipalities by one of 35 measures. It was retired on 2026-11-05 (navigation plan, decision 81): each measure is now a dataset, shaded from Explore, the Catalog or Rankings, and an old link with s=<field> opens the same measure as that dataset.
layers.shade_by.plain_es: Un menú del mapa 2D que coloreaba los 78 municipios según una de 35 medidas. Se retiró el 2026-11-05 (plan de navegación, decisión 81): cada medida es ahora un conjunto de datos que se colorea desde Explorar, el Catálogo o Posiciones, y un enlace antiguo con s=<campo> abre la misma medida como ese conjunto de datos.
layers.shade_by.definition: app.js SHADE_DS lists the 35 fields the menu had and the dataset each now opens, with its scale where the menu used one (tourism places per 1,000 residents or per square kilometer). An address with s=<field> is read when the data of the Analysis tab load (economy.js econInit): the dataset is shaded in five classes, the tab does not change, and the address is rewritten with e=. Eleven of the fields became datasets for this (core/adapters.js SNAPSHOT_FIELDS): nine shares of tourism places near transit, the change in median gross rent since 2008-2012 and Uber's listing (1 or 0).
layers.shade_by.method: app.js SHADE_DS; economy.js econInit; core/adapters.js SNAPSHOT_FIELDS. tests/test_catalog.py checks that every one of the 35 fields opens a dataset.
layers.shade_by.how_to_read: Read the dataset the measure now opens: its legend, its scale and its own dictionary entry.
caveats: The three 'places shown' measures counted only the places the filters let through; their dataset counts every tourism place.
'Population 2020' opens the population dataset, which shows its latest year.
The 14 municipalities with no mapped transit stop have no value for the transit shares of places, not 0%: there is no measurement.

values.assets: Tourism places. Count of places in Snapshot 2026-10 (confidence 0.50 or more, no places of worship).
values.assets_per_1000_residents: Places per 1,000 residents. Places divided by 2020 Census residents, times 1,000.
values.assets_per_km2: Places per km². Places divided by land area in square kilometers.
values.sfha_pct: % of places in flood hazard area. Share of the municipality's places inside a Special Flood Hazard Area.
values.in_sfha: Places in flood hazard area. Count of places.
values.in_protected: Places inside protected areas. Count of places.
values.with_website: Places with a website. Count of places.
values.acc_cur400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable. The nearest stop with a published timetable (ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or a municipal system, in a feed that has not ended) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_freq400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a frequent stop (20+ weekday departures). A stop with a current timetable and 20 or more departures on a typical weekday is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_sat400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Saturday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Saturday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_sun400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Sunday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Sunday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_paper_pct: % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop. A mapped stop is 400 m or less away but none with a current timetable: its timetable has ended, or volunteers mapped it and there is none. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.transit_pct: % of places within 400 m of any mapped stop. The nearest stop, station or terminal of any kind is 400 m or less away in a straight line, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.transit_stops: Transit stops and stations. Count of scheduled stops, OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, Tren Urbano stations and ferry terminals inside the municipality. Airports, taxi stands and electric vehicle chargers are not counted.
values.uber_listed: Uber lists service (yes or no). Two colors: listed or not listed. It is a hand-typed copy of Uber's Puerto Rico cities page checked 2026-10-01 (57 of 78 municipalities listed). A listing, not measured coverage. 'Not listed' does not mean Uber is absent, because Uber says its service reaches beyond the places it lists.
values.affordability_ratio: Housing: affordability ratio. Median home value divided by the largest 30-year loan a household with the median income can carry (30% of income for housing, 78% of that for principal and interest, 5% rate). American Community Survey (ACS) 2020-2024. Above 1 means out of reach.
values.median_home_value: Housing: median home value, in dollars, ACS 2020-2024.
values.median_gross_rent: Housing: median gross rent, in dollars a month, ACS 2020-2024.
values.renter_cost_burden_pct: Housing: share of renter households that pay 30% or more of income on rent, ACS 2020-2024.
values.vacancy_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant, ACS 2020-2024.
values.seasonal_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant seasonal, recreational or occasional-use units, ACS 2020-2024.
values.gross_rent_change_pct: Housing: change in median gross rent from the 2008-2012 window to the 2020-2024 window, in percent. It is not adjusted for inflation. US consumer prices rose 36.6% from 2012 to 2024. In Snapshot 2026-10, 54 of the 78 municipalities changed by less than that (2 of them fell).
values.urban_pct: Land use: % of land classified Suelo Urbano in the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.protected_land_pct: Land use: % of land classified Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido (specially protected rural land) in the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.pop_served_active_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop with a current timetable, in Snapshot 2026-10.
values.pop_served_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop, expired timetables included, in Snapshot 2026-10.

layers.hubs_control.plain: The 'Stations, terminals & airports' switch shows the larger mobility points: bus stations and terminals, Tren Urbano stations, ferry terminals and airports.
layers.hubs_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Estaciones, terminales y aeropuertos" muestra los puntos de movilidad más grandes: estaciones y terminales de guaguas, estaciones del Tren Urbano, terminales de lanchas y aeropuertos.
layers.hubs_control.definition: The layer holds 145 points in Snapshot 2026-10: 91 bus stations and terminals, 16 Tren Urbano stations, 13 ferry terminals and 25 airports and airfields (14 from the list of the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA, and 11 from OpenStreetMap). Icons are larger than stop icons and are not clustered. A click opens the same card as a stop. For an airport the card also says 'Public use' or 'Private use' and gives its codes. The layer is off when the page opens. The 3D view has the same switch: the same points as dots (Tren Urbano red, ferry terminals teal, bus stations and airports charcoal, airports larger), with the same card.
layers.hubs_control.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addHubs): points whose kind is bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal or airport go to this layer. The card is transportPopup in access.js, which both views load.
layers.hubs_control.how_to_read: Use it to see where the main interchange and entry points are. An airport is not a transit stop.
caveats: In Snapshot 2026-10, the card says 'Public use' for every airport that is not marked private. That includes 11 airports from OpenStreetMap, which carry no public-use flag. Only the 14 FAA records state it (10 public use, 4 private use). The names of some OpenStreetMap airfields say closed, historic or military, and one includes 'CERRADO' (closed). The municipality chip counts only FAA airports marked public use, so the chip and the card can differ. Treat OpenStreetMap airfields as mapped, not confirmed open.
A station from OpenStreetMap shows that someone mapped it, not that it is staffed or served today.

The credit line on the map names the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), OpenStreetMap and the FAA. In Snapshot 2026-10, 29 bus stations come from municipal feeds, so credit those feeds too when you cite.
layers.hubs_control.source_detail: transport.json (kinds bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal and airport). Timetable data are from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal feeds in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form. Credit line on the map: 'Stations: ATI GTFS, OpenStreetMap, FAA'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Stations, terminals & airports
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Stations, terminals & airports

layers.taxi_ev_control.plain: The 'Taxi stands & EV charging' switch shows taxi stands and electric vehicle (EV) chargers that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. There are 9 taxi stands and 11 chargers in Snapshot 2026-10.
layers.taxi_ev_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Paradas de taxis y carga de vehículos eléctricos" muestra las paradas de taxis y los cargadores de vehículos eléctricos que personas voluntarias trazaron en OpenStreetMap. Hay 9 paradas de taxis y 11 cargadores en el corte de datos de 2026-10.
layers.taxi_ev_control.definition: The layer reads points of kind taxi, ev_charging, bike_rental and helipad. Snapshot 2026-10 holds only taxi stands and chargers. Click for a card with the name, the kind and the municipality. Ride-hailing is not drawn here. Whether Uber lists a municipality is a yes or no, shown by shading the map by 'Uber lists service' or by the chip on the Municipality tab. The 3D view has the same switch and card; its dots take the color of their kind (taxi stands amber, chargers green).
layers.taxi_ev_control.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addTaxi): kinds in TAXI_KINDS (access.js) go to this layer.
layers.taxi_ev_control.how_to_read: Use it to see where such points are known. It is not a list of all taxis or chargers.
caveats: OpenStreetMap volunteers add these points, so the layer shows what has been mapped (9 taxi stands and 11 chargers in Snapshot 2026-10), not what exists.
Taxi stands and chargers are not scheduled transit and are not counted in the stop totals.
layers.taxi_ev_control.source_detail: transport.json. Credit line on the map: '© OpenStreetMap contributors'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Taxi stands & EV charging
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Taxi stands & EV charging

layers.tourism_places.plain: Tourism places are the pins on the map: attractions, restaurants and bars, places to stay and visitor services listed by Overture Maps. Pins are colored by category, and a dark ring marks a place inside a high-risk flood area mapped by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
layers.tourism_places.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos son los marcadores del mapa: atracciones, restaurantes y bares, lugares para hospedarse y servicios para visitantes que lista Overture Maps. Cada marcador tiene el color de su categoría, y un anillo oscuro señala un lugar dentro de una zona de alto riesgo de inundación según los mapas de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias).
layers.tourism_places.definition: The switch 'Tourism places' is off when the page opens, and the listings are not loaded yet. The label beside the switch says how much they weigh (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10, the listings and their transit access columns together). The first time you switch the layer on, download a municipality's places, search the listings or press 'Load the place listings' in the Municipality tab, the page fetches places.json and place_access.json. The pins are the listings in places.json that pass the current filters: the four category buttons, the minimum confidence slider and the places-of-worship switch. With the defaults the map counts 24,209 of the 32,541 listings in Snapshot 2026-10 (built 2026-10-02) and draws 23,467 of them as pins (holiday rentals are counted, not drawn), and the label beside the switch says how many are shown. Pins join into numbered clusters until zoom level 16. A click on a pin opens a card with the name, the type, the municipality and region, the street address when there is one, badges, links and a source line. The badges are listed below. Links go to the place's website, when it has one, and to OpenStreetMap at the place's location.
layers.tourism_places.method: app.js (ensurePlaces, rebuildPlaces, placePopup) loads the listings on first use and makes one Leaflet marker for each visible place and groups the markers with Leaflet.markercluster: clusters of pins within 55 pixels, no clustering from zoom 16. Each pin is 26 pixels wide and carries the icon of the place type. When a filter changes, the pins are rebuilt in chunks of 4,000 so that the page stays responsive.
layers.tourism_places.how_to_read: A cluster number counts listings under the current filters. A pin is a listing, not a count of visitors or sales. The dark ring says the place's coordinates fall inside a mapped flood zone, not that the building floods. The Cite button of this entry cites the control. To cite the data, use the Cite button on the entries listed under Related, for example places.category.
caveats: Overture listings can be missing, duplicated, closed or out of date. The confidence slider filters them but does not remove every error.

The filters change the pins, the live numbers on the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places download in comma-separated values (CSV) form. They do not change the statistics of each municipality (Rankings tab, shading, municipality download), which use the default filters: confidence 0.50 and no places of worship.

The badges come from point tests made when the data were built. The access class comes from the stored distances, which the nightly transit refresh can update. No badge is recalculated when you change a filter.

Until the listings are loaded, the Municipality tab shows the figures stored for the default filters, the search box offers to load them and the route planner leaves its tourism count out. Loading them is a download of about 3.0 MB compressed (Snapshot 2026-10), which matters on a phone or a slow connection.

values.Flood hazard area, zone <code>: The pin lies in a Special Flood Hazard Area. The badge prints the FEMA zone letter: AE, VE, AO, A or A99. It is a mapped hazard at a point, not an official flood determination (see the flood zone entry).
values.Zone X (0.2% annual chance): The pin lies in the lighter 0.2% annual chance zone. This is not a Special Flood Hazard Area.
values.Protected area: The badge gives the name of the protected area that holds the pin.
values.Transit access (class and distances): A badge names the place's access class: 'Frequent stop within 400 m', 'Stop within 400 m', 'Stop 400–800 m away', 'Only expired or unscheduled stops within 800 m' or 'No stop within 800 m'. Each badge has an icon as well as a color, and hovering over it gives a note: the figures are schedule-based and in a straight line, a stop counts when its timetable has not ended, and real-time service, walking distance, públicos and taxis are not included. Under the badge, the line 'Nearest stop with a current timetable: <distance>' gives the distance and, within 400 m, the weekday departures and the Saturday and Sunday service. When a stop without a current timetable is closer than that stop, a line 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included): <distance>' follows, and hovering over it shows the stop's name. If the access file is missing or does not match the places file, the card shows only the badge 'any mapped stop <distance>'. The classes are described in methods.access_profile.
values.Confidence: Overture's confidence score for the listing, from 0 to 1.
values.Duplicates folded: How many duplicate listings were folded into the place.
values.Source line: Names Overture Maps, the contributing source and the original Overture category.

layers.tourism_places.source_detail: places.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 32,541 listings, 24,209 of them on the default basis. Overture Maps Places release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026. Credit line on the map: 'Places © Overture Maps Foundation'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Tourism places

layers.transit_routes_control.plain: The 'Transit routes' switch draws every public route in the observatory's data. These are the Tren Urbano, buses and ferries of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI, the Integrated Transport Authority), municipal buses and trolleys, and routes mapped in OpenStreetMap. Thicker lines have more weekday trips.
layers.transit_routes_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Rutas de transporte colectivo" dibuja todas las rutas públicas de los datos del observatorio. Son el Tren Urbano, las guaguas y las lanchas de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado), las guaguas y los trolleys municipales, y las rutas trazadas en OpenStreetMap. Las líneas más gruesas tienen más viajes los días de semana.
layers.transit_routes_control.definition: Width grows with the weekday trips of the route, from 2 to 7 pixels. The Tren Urbano is one pixel wider than a bus line with the same trips. Routes mapped in OpenStreetMap are 2.5 pixels wide and ferries 3. Pointing at a line thickens it. A click opens a card with the route name, the operator and network, weekday, Saturday and Sunday trips, the first and last weekday departure, how the line was drawn, the state of the timetable with its dates, and a credit line. The routes load from transit_routes.geojson (about 1.0 MB in Snapshot 2026-10) the first time the switch is on. The colors and line styles are listed below.
layers.transit_routes_control.method: app.js (loadRoutes) and network.js (routeColor, routeStyle, routePopup). width = 2 + 0.7 x log2(1 + weekday trips), at most 7. The 'Show' button of an operator on the Transit tab dims every other operator's lines to 12% opacity.
layers.transit_routes_control.how_to_read: Read a line as a guide to where a route runs. Open its card to see whether its timetable is current, expiring or expired.
caveats: Routes of operators whose timetable has expired stay on the map.
A route in a feed is not proof that the service runs today.
In Snapshot 2026-10, the 16 routes from OpenStreetMap have no timetable, so their trip counts are 0, meaning none published.

values.ATI buses: Blue line. It includes the buses of the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA, the Metropolitan Bus Authority), Metrobús and Metro Urbano.
values.Routes mapped in OpenStreetMap: Gold dashes. In Snapshot 2026-10 there are 16 routes that volunteers mapped: 9 carros públicos and 7 bus or trolley lines. None has a timetable.
values.Solid line: The line follows the operator's own route shape or the road network.
values.Dashed, lighter line: The feed lists the stops out of order, so the visiting order was inferred.
values.Dotted line: No road path was found, so the line joins the stops straight.

layers.transit_routes_control.source_detail: transit_routes.geojson. Timetable feeds are in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format. Credit line on the map: 'Routes: ATI, municipal GTFS feeds, OpenStreetMap'.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Transit routes

layers.transit_stops_control.plain: The 'Transit stops' switch shows boarding points: scheduled stops from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and from municipal timetable feeds in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form, plus bus stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. The number beside the switch counts them.
layers.transit_stops_control.plain_es: El interruptor "Paradas de transporte colectivo" muestra los puntos donde se aborda: paradas con horario de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) y de los horarios municipales en formato GTFS (formato estándar de horarios de transporte colectivo), además de paradas de guaguas que personas voluntarias trazaron en OpenStreetMap. El número junto al interruptor las cuenta.
layers.transit_stops_control.definition: The layer holds the points of kind transit_stop (scheduled stops, 3,781 in Snapshot 2026-10) and bus_stop (OpenStreetMap stops that are not within 30 meters of a scheduled stop, 459), 4,240 in all. The 3,781 are the scheduled stops that are not stations. In Snapshot 2026-10 there are 3,847 scheduled stops in all. The other 66 are bus stations, ferry terminals and Tren Urbano stations, and they appear on the stations layer. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads transport.json (about 1.3 MB in Snapshot 2026-10), which the stations and taxi layers share. Points join into numbered blue clusters until zoom 15. A click opens a card with the stop's name, kind and municipality, the routes and modes that call there, weekday departures, a weekend line ('Weekend departures: Saturday N · Sunday N', with 'none listed' for a day that has no departures, or 'No weekend departures in the published timetable' when neither day has any; scheduled stops only), the end date of the stop's timetable ('Timetable valid until' a date, or 'Timetable ended' with a warning sign when the date has passed), the operator, a note when the source says wheelchair boarding is possible, and a source line. The 400 m walk rings use these points. The 3D view has the same switch, in the same group: the same points, in blue clusters that give their count up to zoom 14 and as single dots from zoom 15, with the same card (a click on a cluster zooms in).
layers.transit_stops_control.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addStops); the card is transportPopup in access.js, which both views load. The clusters group points within 40 pixels, in both views.
layers.transit_stops_control.how_to_read: Check the source line first. A scheduled stop appears in a published timetable. An OpenStreetMap stop only shows that someone mapped a stop there.
caveats: Stops of operators whose timetable has expired stay on the map.
OpenStreetMap stops can be missing, out of date or wrong. The observatory does not check them on the ground.

The credit line on the map names ATI and OpenStreetMap only. In Snapshot 2026-10, 2,381 of the 3,781 scheduled stops come from municipal feeds, so credit both when you cite. The stop card's type label reads 'Transit stop (ATI)' for every scheduled stop, municipal ones included. The source line at the bottom of the card names the actual feed.

The card says 'wheelchair accessible' only when the source states that boarding is possible (feed field wheelchair_boarding = 1, or OpenStreetMap tag wheelchair=yes).
