Data management: published data files
Data management: growth
Data management: what is not published
Data management: definitions

layers.housing_dialog.plain: A 'Full data' window shows one dataset in full. It lists every municipality and Puerto Rico, every year and the margins of error where published. It has a trend chart and a download of the data as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
layers.housing_dialog.plain_es: Una ventana de "Datos completos" muestra un conjunto de datos completo. Enumera cada municipio y Puerto Rico, cada año y los márgenes de error cuando se publican. Tiene una gráfica de tendencia y permite descargar los datos como archivo CSV (valores separados por comas).
layers.housing_dialog.definition: Open it with a 'Full data' button, a latest-data number, a row label in the profile, a dataset in the catalog or the link ?d=. The window shows tags, the definition, the source (linked), the table reference and a note on the years (American Community Survey (ACS) windows, the population basis or the disasters of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, FEMA). It adds a note on margins of error (±, 90% confidence) and, for a series, a 'Full entry' link to its entry in the data dictionary. Published tables open the same window with their rows and a CSV file. The file is pr_housing_<name>.csv. The codes below describe the tools, the chart and the table.
layers.housing_dialog.method: housing.js (openDataset, openStatic, renderDsTable, renderDsChart, dsCsv). The address gets ?d=<dataset> while the dialog is open.
layers.housing_dialog.how_to_read: Use the window to find the exact value and its margin. Cite the value with its survey window.
caveats: Italics warn of low reliability. They are shown whether or not margins are switched on.

values.Tools: A box to find a municipality, a switch 'Show margin of error (±)', the count of municipalities and years, and 'Download CSV'.
values.Trend chart: Draws the ticked municipalities (up to 8). Puerto Rico and the selected municipality are ticked at the start.
values.Table: Puerto Rico first, then the 78 municipalities by name, one column for each year. A click on a column heading sorts by it. The column of the selected year is highlighted. A value whose margin of error is more than 30% of the estimate is shown in italics.

view.label: Housing page: median gross rent, full data

layers.housing_headline_numbers.plain: The top of the Housing page has two rows of large numbers. 'Latest data' has eight live Puerto Rico figures that open their full data. 'As published in the 2023 study' has six printed figures.
layers.housing_headline_numbers.plain_es: La parte superior de la página de Vivienda tiene dos filas de números grandes. "Datos más recientes" tiene ocho cifras actualizadas de Puerto Rico que abren sus datos completos. "Tal como se publicó en el estudio de 2023" tiene seis cifras impresas.
layers.housing_headline_numbers.definition: Latest data holds eight figures. They are residents (population), the change since the 2020 census, housing units and the share of homes vacant. They also include 'other vacant' homes (the abandoned-housing proxy), the median home value, the share of renters who pay 30% or more of income on rent, and the affordability ratio (above 1 means out of reach). Each shows its source and year and opens its full data. As published holds five figures: housing units in 2020 (1.6 million), vacant homes in 2020 and the estimate of dilapidated or abandoned units. The others are the new homes needed each year (a government estimate) and the residents of the 2020 census (3,285,694).
layers.housing_headline_numbers.method: housing.js (renderLatestKpis, renderPaperTables). The printed numbers are in housing.json.
layers.housing_headline_numbers.how_to_read: Compare a live figure with its printed partner only when they describe the same thing and year.
caveats: Printed estimates (abandoned units, new homes needed) are the study's own estimates. They are not recalculated.
The printed 2020 residents figure (3,285,694) is 180 lower than the 2020 census count in the live series (3,285,874). The page shows both figures as their sources give them.

The printed 370,000 vacant homes is labeled Census 2020 on the page, but the 2020 census-day count of vacant units in the observatory's data is 257,625. The printed figure is close to survey estimates (368,182 for the 2015-2019 window). Treat it as the study's figure.

view.label: Housing page: headline numbers

layers.housing_change_measure.plain: Four maps on the Housing page show change since a base year. They cover median home value, median gross rent, median household income and the share of adults with a bachelor's degree.
layers.housing_change_measure.plain_es: Cuatro mapas de la página de Vivienda muestran el cambio desde un año base. Cubren la mediana del valor de la vivienda, la mediana del alquiler bruto, la mediana del ingreso del hogar y la proporción de personas adultas con bachillerato.
layers.housing_change_measure.definition: For home value, rent and income the value is the percent change: (value in the selected year minus value in the base year) divided by the value in the base year, times 100, rounded to two decimals. For the bachelor's share it is the difference in percentage points. Dollars are not adjusted for inflation. The base year is chosen in the year bar and starts at 2012, the window 2008-2012. Only years after the base year have a value. The page calls these maps 'change, base → year'. The same numbers fill the change rows of the municipality profile.
layers.housing_change_measure.method: housing.js (CHANGE, indexSeries). The values are calculated in the browser from the American Community Survey (ACS) series, so they follow the base year.
layers.housing_change_measure.how_to_read: A positive percentage means the value rose in dollars of its own year. Part of a rise in prices or rents is general inflation.
caveats: Not inflation-adjusted. Use the Analysis tab's inflation option for constant dollars.
Windows that overlap share most of their sample. Pick a base year at least five years before the selected year for real change.
The change fields in the municipality statistics use a fixed base of 2008-2012 and the latest window. These maps follow the base you choose.
layers.housing_change_measure.source_detail: housing_series.json (median_home_value, median_gross_rent, median_hh_income and bachelors_pct, calculated in your browser) and municipios.geojson. The maps have no credit line. The tag beside each title names the source.

view.label: Housing page: change in rent, base 2012, 2022

layers.housing_catalog.plain: The Data section lists every dataset on the Housing page. Type in the box to find one, and press a name to open its full data.
layers.housing_catalog.plain_es: La sección "Datos" enumera todos los conjuntos de datos de la página de Vivienda. Escriba en la caja para encontrar uno y oprima un nombre para abrir sus datos completos.
layers.housing_catalog.definition: The catalog lists 58 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: 46 survey, census, estimate and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) series, 3 land-use shares and 9 published or island-wide tables. Groups are Population, Housing stock, Households, Prices and incomes, Cost burden, Affordability, Disaster recovery and Land use, and then 'Published tables and island-wide series'. Each row gives the name, the source reference, the years it covers and a note when margins of error are published. The box 'Find a dataset' looks in the name, the reference and the group, ignoring accents and capitals, and the count beside it shows how many datasets match.
layers.housing_catalog.how_to_read: Use the group names to browse. Use the box when you know a word such as rent or vacancy.
caveats: The catalog counts datasets of this page. The Analysis tab lists more datasets and groups them differently.

view.label: Housing page: Data

layers.housing_affordability_scatter.plain: A chart plots each municipality's median household income against its median home value. A line marks where the typical home exactly equals the largest loan a household with that income can carry.
layers.housing_affordability_scatter.plain_es: Una gráfica compara la mediana del ingreso del hogar de cada municipio con la mediana del valor de su vivienda. Una línea marca dónde la vivienda típica es exactamente igual al préstamo más grande que puede asumir un hogar con ese ingreso.
layers.housing_affordability_scatter.definition: Each dot is a municipality, for the survey window of the chosen year (the title says which). A red dot sits above the line: its median home value is higher than the maximum affordable loan for its median income. A green dot sits below the line. The line is drawn from zero income to 5% above the highest income. It uses the study's arithmetic: 30% of income for housing, 78% of that to principal and interest, a 30-year loan at a fixed 5%. A click on a dot selects the municipality. The chart's legend names the three marks.
layers.housing_affordability_scatter.how_to_read: Dots far above the line are municipalities where typical homes cost much more than typical incomes can borrow for.
caveats: The loan rate is fixed at 5% in every year. The Housing page notes that actual mortgage rates ranged from under 4% to over 7% over this period.
Median values and median incomes come from a survey with margins of error that are large in small municipalities.
The line is a screening test. It is not a lending rule and it ignores down payments, taxes and insurance.

view.label: Housing page: Home ownership affordability

layers.housing_maps.plain: Each housing variable has a map of the 78 municipalities and a ranked bar chart. Colors show five groups whose limits come from all years together, so the same color means the same number in every year.
layers.housing_maps.plain_es: Cada variable de vivienda tiene un mapa de los 78 municipios y una gráfica de barras ordenada. Los colores muestran cinco grupos cuyos límites salen de todos los años juntos, así que el mismo color significa el mismo número en todos los años.
layers.housing_maps.definition: Each block has a title with a year chip, the source tag, a '?' help button and a 'Full data' button. A line gives the median, lowest and highest of the 78 municipalities and the Puerto Rico value. Below are a map, a readout for the selected municipality with its rank, a bar chart of all 78 municipalities (highest first) and a legend with the number of municipalities in each class. The class limits are the quintiles of the 78 municipalities over every year of the variable together, except on the five diverging maps (see the codes below). Because of that, the groups are not equal in size in one year: in Snapshot 2026-10, for median gross rent in 2024, the five groups hold 1, 3, 9, 26 and 39 municipalities. Municipalities with no value are pale gray. The maps have no base map, do not zoom with the wheel and, on a touch device, do not drag. The codes below list the 28 maps by section, the diverging maps and the selection.
layers.housing_maps.method: housing.js (buildViz, updateViz, pooled, colorFor, legendHTML). A map is built when it comes within about 800 pixels of the screen.
layers.housing_maps.how_to_read: Read the legend for the numbers. The color classes do not change with the year, so a municipality can change color as its value moves.
caveats: Ranks and medians count only municipalities with a value. Tied values share the first of their places.
Survey estimates for small municipalities carry large margins of error. The readout shows the margin (±) when the survey publishes one.

values.Selection and hover: A click on a municipality on the map, or on a bar, selects it. The selected municipality is outlined in dark gray on every map, and the profile and readouts follow. Pointing at a municipality shows its name, value, rank and the source tag.
values.Diverging maps: Five maps use a diverging scale around 0: the four change maps (home value, gross rent, household income and bachelor's share) and the population-change map. The class limits are −50%, −10%, +10% and +50% of the largest absolute value over all years: below −50%, −50% to −10%, within ±10%, +10% to +50% and above +50% of that value. For population change the largest value is 39.05% in the 2026-10 snapshot. Blue is an increase and red is a decrease. Neither means better or worse. The limits of the four change maps depend on the base year chosen in the year bar.
values.Section 2, housing stock: vacancy_pct, other_vacant_pct, seasonal_pct, rental_vacancy_pct, overcrowded_pct, residents_per_unit.
values.Section 6, short-term rentals and the ma: The four change maps: gross_rent_change_pct, home_value_change_pct, income_change_pct, bachelors_change_pts. They are calculated in your browser from the survey series and follow the base year. They share names with fields of municipalities.json, which use a fixed base.
values.Section 10, land use: urban_pct, urbanizable_pct, protected_land_pct. These read municipalities.json and show one year, 2015.

layers.housing_maps.source_detail: housing_series.json (the 21 survey, census, estimate and recovery series, and the four change maps calculated from them), municipalities.json (the three land-use maps) and municipios.geojson (the outlines). The maps have no base map and carry no credit line. The tag beside each title names the source.

view.label: Housing page: Home ownership affordability

layers.housing_profile.plain: The Municipality profile shows the study's Table 11 variables and the housing indicators for any municipality and year. Pick one from the menu or click any map.
layers.housing_profile.plain_es: El "Perfil del municipio" muestra las variables de la Tabla 11 del estudio y los indicadores de vivienda de cualquier municipio y año. Elija uno en el menú o haga clic en cualquier mapa.
layers.housing_profile.definition: The menu lists the 78 municipalities in alphabetical order. The page opens on Ceiba, the study's case, unless the link names another. The left card holds the study's Table 11 variables and the Data Observatory's tourism supply. The right card has six groups of housing indicators. Each row has the label (press it for the full data), the rank among the 78 ('#n of 78'), the value with its margin, a small trend line with its length and, when the year differs, the year. A caution appears for municipalities with fewer than 25,000 residents. A link opens the municipality in the Data Observatory. The codes below list the rows of each card.
layers.housing_profile.method: housing.js (selectMuni, row, spark). The tourism and land-use rows read municipalities.json.
layers.housing_profile.how_to_read: Use the rank and the trend line to place a municipality, and the margin to judge a small difference.
caveats: Ranks count only municipalities with a value. Tied values share the first of their places.
The affordability line says 'out of reach' when the rounded ratio is above 1. It uses the study's fixed 5% loan rate in every year.
Housing assistance from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) counts approvals of owners and renters, not damaged homes.

In Snapshot 2026-10, 14 municipalities have no stop counted inside the border (for example Isabela, Yauco and Maricao). For them the card shows 0.0% of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable and of any mapped stop, or 0.4% and 0.8% for Toa Alta and Arroyo. That means no stop was counted inside the municipality, not that no place is near transit. The 2D map leaves the share near any mapped stop blank for them.
The table numbers are those used on this page and in this dictionary. The study PDF numbers some tables differently (the Ceiba table is Table 13 in the PDF and Table 11 here).

values.Left card: People: Population, change since the 2010 census, aged 65 and over, median age, median household income, adults with a bachelor's degree, employment rate for ages 16 and over and population below the poverty level.
values.Left card: Tourism supply: The Data Observatory's tourism places, the share in a flood hazard area of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the share within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable and the share within 400 m of any mapped stop. These are the stored values, which use the default filters.
values.Right card: Stock: Housing units, vacant, seasonal, 'other vacant', rental vacancy, overcrowded and residents per unit.
values.Right card: Prices and burden: Median home value and rent, cost-burdened renters, severely cost-burdened renters and cost-burdened owners with a mortgage.
values.Right card: Affordability (Table 6 metho: Maximum affordable 30-year loan, affordability ratio with 'out of reach' or 'within reach', and owner-occupied share.
values.Right card: Change from the base year: Rent, home value, income and bachelor's share.
values.Right card: Disaster recovery: FEMA housing-assistance households over all disasters.
values.Right card: Land use: Urban, urbanizable and protected shares, and tourism places on protected rural land.

view.label: Housing page: profile of Ceiba
Housing page: profile of Ponce, 2020

layers.housing_published_tables.plain: The Housing page shows Tables 2, 6, 7 and 10 of the 2023 study as printed, and for Tables 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 a live version for the chosen year beside them. The table numbers are those used on this page and in this dictionary. The study PDF numbers some tables differently (for example the affordability table is Table 8 in the PDF and Table 6 here).
layers.housing_published_tables.plain_es: La página de Vivienda muestra las Tablas 2, 6, 7 y 10 del estudio de 2023 tal como se publicaron y, al lado de las Tablas 2, 3, 4, 6 y 7, una versión actualizada para el año elegido. Los números de tabla son los que se usan en esta página y en este diccionario. El PDF del estudio numera algunas tablas de otra forma (por ejemplo, la tabla de asequibilidad es la Tabla 8 en el PDF y la Tabla 6 aquí).
layers.housing_published_tables.definition: The page shows Tables 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 of the 2023 study as printed, with the table numbers used on this page. For Tables 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 it adds a live version for the chosen year, built from the American Community Survey (ACS) or from the Census Bureau's population estimates. Each table has a button to open the full table in the 'Full data' window. Printed and live versions use different years and methods. These ids work in the link ?d= (see the codes below).
layers.housing_published_tables.how_to_read: Read a printed table and its live version together. They use different years and methods.
caveats: The study's change columns compare 2012 with 2021 in nominal dollars. The live columns compare the base year with the chosen year, also nominal. The two can differ in sign. They are different measurements, not corrections of each other.
Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) projects are shown as printed in the 2023 study. The table is not updated from the database of the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
Locations on the LIHTC map are at the municipality, not at the project.

The cost and Community Development Block Grant for Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) amounts in Table 10 are estimates printed in the 2023 study and are not updated. They are the study's estimates, not a record of spending.

values.population: Table 2, Puerto Rico's population change. Two menus 'Compare ... with ...' pick any two population years, and a line of the table uses them. The page also shows the study's printed figures and the census counts of 2010 and 2020.
values.table6: Table 6 as printed: maximum home loan by age of householder, 2021. The page repeats the same arithmetic for the chosen year's incomes.
values.t6live: Table 6 method for every ACS window: median income by age of householder and the maximum 30-year mortgage.
values.table7: Table 7: owner-occupied units by age of householder, as printed and for every ACS window. A chart shows the printed shares beside the chosen year.
values.table10: Table 10: LIHTC projects funded with CDBG-DR, as printed. A map shows one circle for each municipality, sized by units. The cost and CDBG-DR amounts are estimates printed in the 2023 study and are not updated.
values.grapilive: Table 3, live: gross rent as a share of income, every ACS window, island-wide (ACS table B25070). A chart shows the distribution for the chosen year, with the share paying 30% or more in red. The study's figure (52% of renters) is beside it.
values.smocapilive: Table 4, live: owner costs as a share of income with a mortgage, every ACS window, island-wide (ACS table B25091). A chart shows the distribution for the chosen year, with the share paying 30% or more in red. The study's figure (38% of owners with a mortgage) is beside it.

layers.housing_page.plain: The Housing page reproduces key tables of the 2023 study 'The State of Housing in Puerto Rico' by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR), as printed. It also adds live data for all 78 municipalities, 2010 to 2025 in Snapshot 2026-10. The live data come from Census Bureau population estimates (through 2025), American Community Survey (ACS) windows (through 2020-2024) and housing assistance figures from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
layers.housing_page.plain_es: La página de Vivienda reproduce tablas clave del estudio de 2023 "El estado de la vivienda en Puerto Rico", de Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR), tal como se publicaron. También agrega datos actualizados de los 78 municipios, de 2010 a 2025 en el corte de datos de 2026-10. Estos datos provienen de los estimados de población del Negociado del Censo, hasta 2025; de los periodos de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad (ACS), hasta 2020-2024; y de las cifras de asistencia de vivienda de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias).
layers.housing_page.definition: A contents bar lists 13 sections: Headline, Population, Housing stock, Cost burden, Affordability, Ownership, Rent and value change, Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC), Recovery, Municipality profile, Land use, Data and Sources. A year bar below it moves every map, chart and table. The page holds 28 maps, each with a ranked chart, plus charts and tables. Maps and charts are built when you scroll near them. Published figures carry the tag 'study'. Live figures carry the Census Bureau's survey and year, shown as tags, listed below. A click on a municipality on any map loads its profile. A sources section lists every source with its license and the way to cite the page. Without JavaScript the page cannot draw its maps, charts and tables. The top bar links to the 2D map, the 3D view and the data dictionary, and the 'Full data' window of a series links to that series' entry in the dictionary.
layers.housing_page.method: housing.js reads data/housing_series.json (built by housing_series.py), housing.json (the study's tables), municipalities.json and municipios.geojson. Charts use Chart.js and the maps use Leaflet, without a base map.
layers.housing_page.how_to_read: Check the tag before you cite a figure. A 'study' tag means printed in 2023. A survey tag means a live figure for that window.
caveats: The page reproduces Tables 2, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 and the headline figures of the study as printed. Other tables of the study are not reproduced as printed here. The entry on published tables gives the details.
The table numbers are those used on this page and in this dictionary. The study PDF numbers some tables differently (for example the affordability table is Table 8 in the PDF and Table 6 here).

values.study: Tag on a published figure: reproduced as printed in the 2023 study (© Foundation for Puerto Rico 2023).
values.ACS 2020-2024: Tag on a survey figure: the American Community Survey 5-year window shown, labeled by its last year. Windows run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024.
values.Census 2020: Tag on an April 1 figure. For housing units and for the 2010 population it is the census count. For population in 2020 it is the Census Bureau's April 1, 2020 estimates base, not the census file (see the entry on resident population).
values.Estimate 2025: Tag on a Census Bureau population estimate for July 1.
values.FEMA 2022: Tag on a FEMA figure: the year of the disaster declaration.
values.PUT 2015: Tag on a land-use share: the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.

layers.housing_page.source_detail: housing.html, with housing_series.json (built by housing_series.py), housing.json (the study's tables), municipalities.json and municipios.geojson. American Community Survey 5-year detailed tables used, as listed on the page: B01002, B01003, B15002, B17001, B19013, B19049, B19301, B23025, B25001, B25002, B25003, B25004, B25007, B25010, B25014, B25024, B25035, B25064, B25070, B25071, B25077, B25088, B25091 and B25119. Housing units, occupied and vacant for 2010 and 2020 come from table H1 of the Public Law (PL) 94-171 redistricting files. Housing assistance comes from OpenFEMA. The page's own citation reads: Foundation for Puerto Rico, FPR Research in Data: The State of Housing in Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, <snapshot label>, https://observatory.foundationpr.org/housing.html. The maps on this page have no base map and carry no credit line. The tag beside each title names the source.

layers.housing_year_bar.plain: The year bar at the top of the Housing page moves every map, chart and table to the chosen year. 'Change measured from' sets the base year for the change maps.
layers.housing_year_bar.plain_es: La barra de años en la parte superior de la página de Vivienda lleva cada mapa, gráfica y tabla al año elegido. "Cambio medido desde" fija el año base de los mapas de cambio.
layers.housing_year_bar.definition: The bar has previous and next buttons, a year list ('Latest', then 2025 down to 2010 in Snapshot 2026-10), a slider over the same years and a Play button. Play starts at 2010, or at the chosen year, moves one year every 1.3 seconds up to the last year and stops. Choosing a year by hand stops it. Changing the base year does not. In Snapshot 2026-10 the base year list holds 2010 to 2023 and starts at 2012. It sets the base of the change maps and the change rows of the profile. Each dataset shows the same year when it has one, otherwise its latest earlier year (the chip says 'latest at or before 2021') or, if the year is before it starts, its first year (the chip says 'first data'). The published tables as printed and the land-use maps (a 2015 plan) do not change with the year. The year, the base year and the municipality are kept in the page address.
layers.housing_year_bar.how_to_read: Read the chip next to a map title for the year it really shows.
caveats: American Community Survey (ACS) years are five-year windows labeled by their last year. Neighboring windows share four of five years of sample, so compare windows that do not overlap (2012, 2017, 2022) for real change.
In Snapshot 2026-10 the 2021–2025 window is not published yet (the page expects it in December 2026), so 2025 shows the 2020-2024 window for ACS data.

Population is the 2010 census count (April 1, 2010), the April 1, 2020 base of the Census Bureau's latest estimates (the page tags it 'Census 2020') and July 1 estimates in other years. The 2020 base equals the census count for the island but differs from it by 1 to 31 people in 68 of the 78 municipalities in the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.Note beside the bar: For 'Latest' it names each dataset's own latest year (population 2025, ACS 2020-2024). For a year after the latest survey it says that the ACS window for that year is not published yet, that the maps show 2020-2024, and that population is that year's estimate. For any other year it gives the ACS window that ends in it and the July 1 population estimate.

layers.knowledge_area.plain: The Knowledge Area gathers Foundation for Puerto Rico's research and program tools, a home page that lists them all and a header on each page with an 'All areas' menu: Housing, WCRP, Route analysis, Global Innovation Index, Women in the labor force, How public money moves, FEMA disaster funding and need, Budget and public spending, Federal grants: balances, reductions and audit findings, Urban heat, Inflation, Reservoirs, Broadband gaps, Energy, Opportunity Zones 2.0 and Connections between municipios. WCRP, Route analysis, Global Innovation Index, FEMA disaster funding and need, Budget and public spending, Federal grants: balances, reductions and audit findings, Urban heat, Inflation, Reservoirs, Broadband gaps, Energy and Connections between municipios keep a small 'In review' marker in the menu and on their page, with a notice at the top, because their content may still change.
layers.knowledge_area.plain_es: El Área de conocimiento reúne las investigaciones y herramientas de programas de Foundation for Puerto Rico, una página de inicio que las lista todas y un encabezado en cada página con un menú "Todas las áreas": Vivienda, WCRP, Análisis de ruta, Índice Global de Innovación, Mujeres en la fuerza laboral, Cómo se mueve el dinero público, Fondos de FEMA por desastres y necesidad, Presupuesto y gasto público, Subvenciones federales: saldos, reducciones y hallazgos de auditoría, Calor urbano, Inflación, Embalses, Dónde falta banda ancha, Energía, Zonas de Oportunidad 2.0 y Conexiones entre municipios. WCRP, Análisis de ruta, Índice Global de Innovación, Fondos de FEMA por desastres y necesidad, Presupuesto y gasto público, Subvenciones federales: saldos, reducciones y hallazgos de auditoría, Calor urbano, Inflación, Embalses, Dónde falta banda ancha, Energía y Conexiones entre municipios conservan una pequeña marca "En revisión" en el menú y en su página, con un aviso arriba, porque su contenido aún puede cambiar.
layers.knowledge_area.definition: The 'Knowledge' button of the top bar opens the Knowledge home page (knowledge.html): one card for every published area, grouped by topic, with its kind (FPR study, analysis, program tool or index profile), whether it is in review and by whom, the month it was updated, the other topics it belongs to and the published datasets it uses, with a search box and filters. On each area page, the bar below the top bar starts with a header: 'Knowledge' (back to the home page), the area's topic (it opens that topic on the map), an 'All areas' menu that lists every area that is not hidden, grouped by topic, whether the area is in review and by whom, and the month it was updated; the page's own sections follow. The areas, in the order of the menu: Housing (housing.html, published), WCRP (wcrp.html, published, marked 'In review'), Route analysis (route-analysis.html, published, marked 'In review') Global Innovation Index (gii.html, published, marked 'In review'), Women in the labor force (women-labor.html, published), FEMA disaster funding and need (public-money.html, published, marked 'In review'), Budget and public spending (public-spending.html, published, marked 'In review'), Federal grants: balances, reductions and audit findings (unused-funds.html, published, marked 'In review'), Urban heat (urban-heat.html, published, marked 'In review'), Inflation (inflation.html, published, marked 'In review', under Economy), Reservoirs (reservoirs.html, published, marked 'In review', under Infrastructure), Broadband gaps (broadband.html, published, marked 'In review', under Infrastructure), Energy (energy.html, published, marked 'In review', under Infrastructure), Opportunity Zones 2.0 (opportunity-zones.html, published, under Economy) and Connections between municipios (transit-links.html, published, marked 'In review', under Infrastructure). The tab of the page you are on is highlighted. A tab in review carries the marker 'In review'. The page of an area in review shows only a short message that the area is in review, with links to Housing and to the map, and asks search engines not to index it. A published area may keep the marker for a while after its content is approved: its page shows its content with a notice at the top that it is in review and may change, and it also asks search engines not to index it. An area is published (with or without the marker), in review or hidden (no tab).
layers.knowledge_area.method: Every Knowledge Area page draws its tabs from one list in js/core/knowledge.js, and the Knowledge home page draws its cards from js/knowledge_items.js; knowledge.py writes both from the Knowledge registry (knowledge_src/items.json) (each area's id, name in English and Spanish, icon, page, status and, for a published area that keeps the marker, review), with no data file to fetch. A new area needs one entry in that list and its page.
layers.knowledge_area.how_to_read: An area marked 'In review' is either an area that is not published yet (its page has no data) or a published area whose content may still change (its page says so at the top).

data.gazetteer_search.plain: Search finds names that start with, or contain, the words you type, ignoring accents and capital letters. It also expands common abbreviations in what you type, such as 'av' to 'avenida'.
data.gazetteer_search.plain_es: La búsqueda encuentra los nombres que empiezan con las palabras escritas o que las contienen, sin importar acentos ni mayúsculas. También completa abreviaturas comunes en lo que se escribe, como "av" por "avenida".
data.gazetteer_search.definition: The search boxes in the header and in the route planner ask the place-name index, in your browser. A typed text is cleaned, optionally read as a highway number or as coordinates, matched to names and ranked.
data.gazetteer_search.method: 1. Clean the text: remove accents, change to lower case, turn the marks . , ; : ( ) " ' into spaces. 2. If the whole text is pr, ruta, route, carr, carretera, hwy or highway followed by a number of up to 4 digits and an optional letter (for example 'pr 52', 'carr52' or 'highway 52'), it becomes 'pr-52'. Longer text such as 'pr 52 caguas' is not changed this way. 3. Expand words one by one: av, ave, avda to avenida; cll to calle; carr, ctra to carretera; urb to urbanizacion; bo to barrio; res to residencial; hosp to hospital; univ to universidad; pza to plaza; mt to monte. 4. Score each name: 0 exact match; 1 starts with the text; 2 every typed word starts a word of the name; 3 every typed word appears somewhere in the name; no match otherwise. 5. Rank by score, with a small advantage for some types (a municipality ranks ahead of a street); equal scores go to the name nearest the map center, then to the shorter name. 6. Keep up to 4 rows with the same name and type for streets and highways (6 for other types). The combined list shows at most 12 results, with at most 4 streets, 3 highways, 5 tourism places, 4 stops and 4 of any other type. 7. Two numbers that each have at least two decimals, separated by a comma or a space (for example 18.40, -66.05), are read as latitude and longitude, latitude first. Search starts at 2 characters.
data.gazetteer_search.how_to_read: Type a part of the name. If a name is stored with an abbreviation, type another word from it. If nothing matches, try fewer words. Names with equal scores are listed nearest to the map center first, so move the map near the place you want. For a street address, use the online lookup. To search by coordinates, type latitude first, then longitude, each with at least 2 decimals.
caveats: Abbreviations are expanded in what you type, not in the stored names. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 66 stored names contain a word that search expands, such as 'Av.', 'Urb.' or 'Bo.' (for example 'Urb. Marbella'). Typing that word does not find them, because the typed word is expanded and the stored word is not. Typing another word from the name does.
Matching is exact on letters. A misspelling finds nothing.

Online address lookup is optional. It runs only when you choose 'Look up as an address online', which appears after 4 or more characters. It sends the text you typed to the OpenStreetMap Nominatim service, which has its own usage policy. The request also sends your IP address and browser details to the OpenStreetMap server. Nothing else you type leaves the page.
Besides the index, the search boxes also look at the page's own data: tourism places (under the current filters), scheduled stops, stations and terminals, and, in the header box only, transit routes.

data.gazetteer_build.plain: The index starts from names in OpenStreetMap and adds Census rows for municipalities and barrios. Each name gets a municipality. A street that is mapped in several pieces lying in different municipalities gets a row in each.
data.gazetteer_build.plain_es: El índice parte de los nombres de OpenStreetMap y agrega filas del Censo para los municipios y los barrios. Cada nombre recibe un municipio. Una calle mapeada en varios pedazos que caen en municipios distintos tiene una fila en cada uno.
data.gazetteer_build.definition: gazetteer.py turns the OpenStreetMap extract and the published boundaries into rows [name, latitude, longitude, kind, municipality, note].
data.gazetteer_build.method: 1. Read OpenStreetMap nodes and ways that have a name and a matching tag. Place tags (town, city, village, hamlet, suburb, neighborhood, quarter, locality, island, islet) are read from points only. Ways that are not roads are placed at the average of their corner points. 2. Add one row for each municipality and each barrio in the published boundaries. 3. Give each name its municipality by point-in-polygon (checking which boundary contains the point) on the municipality boundaries. A point offshore (a pier or a cay) goes to the nearest municipality when it is within about 2 km (0.02 degree); any other name outside every municipality is dropped. 4. For roads, give each way to the municipality that holds its middle point (the middle mapped point by count of points, not by length). Group ways by name and municipality, place the row at that middle point of the longest piece, and drop street names whose pieces total less than 60 m. A road with a Puerto Rico (PR) route number but no name is also read. Route numbers are taken from the ref tag (the first one, for example PR-52, with an optional letter) and grouped the same way, with the road's local name as the note. Highway numbers are not dropped for length. 5. Drop exact repeats: the same name (ignoring accents and capitals), the same type, and latitude and longitude that are equal when rounded to 3 decimals (cells of about 110 m). 6. Sort by type, then name, round coordinates to 5 decimals and write the file.
data.gazetteer_build.how_to_read: A road has one point for each municipality in which the middle point of one of its mapped pieces lies, placed at the middle point of its longest piece there, so the point may not be where you expect. In the 2026-10 snapshot the boundaries give 78 municipality rows and 901 barrio rows.
caveats: The index uses the OpenStreetMap 'name' tag only. Alternative names and translations are not read.
Place polygons mapped as relations are not read.
Place tags (town, city, village, hamlet, suburb, neighborhood, quarter, locality, island, islet) are read from points only. A place mapped only as an area (a closed way) is not in the index.
The note on a place is the OpenStreetMap place type, for example hamlet or suburb. It is not an official classification.
data.gazetteer_build.geography: Puerto Rico: 78 municipalities, with places on Vieques, Culebra and Mona Island
data.gazetteer_build.source_detail: gazetteer.py (read, main); municipality boundaries from US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K) and barrio boundaries from TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K), both shoreline-clipped (municipios.geojson, barrios.geojson)

data.gazetteer.plain: A list of named places, streets, highway numbers and landmarks (48,450 names in the 2026-10 snapshot), each with a point on the map. The search boxes and the route planner look names up in it, inside your browser.
data.gazetteer.plain_es: Una lista de lugares con nombre, calles, números de carretera y puntos de referencia (48,450 nombres en el corte de datos de 2026-10), cada uno con un punto en el mapa. Los buscadores y el planificador de rutas buscan los nombres en ella, dentro del propio navegador.
data.gazetteer.definition: The file has three parts. 'munis' lists the 78 municipality names in alphabetical order. 'kinds' lists the 19 type codes in a fixed order. 'items' lists the names. Each item is [name, latitude, longitude, kind number, municipality number] with an optional sixth value, a note. The kind number and the municipality number are positions in the 'kinds' and 'munis' lists. Items are sorted by kind, then by name without accents.
data.gazetteer.method: gazetteer.py reads named points and ways from the OpenStreetMap extract, adds the municipality and barrio boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGERweb generalized 500k, shoreline-clipped), gives each name its municipality by point-in-polygon (checking which boundary contains the point), and writes one compact file. The entries on kinds and on how the index is built give the rules.
data.gazetteer.how_to_read: The index holds names with one point each. It has no house numbers or postal addresses. It does not hold the tourism listings; the pages search those separately.
caveats: Names are as OpenStreetMap volunteers wrote them. Spelling, capital letters and abbreviations vary.
Only OpenStreetMap points and ways are read. A place mapped only as a multi-part area (a relation) is missing.
Place tags (place=village, hamlet, suburb, neighbourhood, island and so on) are read from points only. A place mapped only as an area (a closed way) is not in the index.

A road name has one row for each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of its mapped pieces (OpenStreetMap ways). A road mapped as several pieces usually has a row in each municipality it crosses. A single piece that crosses a boundary counts only where its middle point lies, so a long road mapped as one piece has one row.
A road or place that is not mapped with a name in OpenStreetMap is not in the index.

License: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. Credit line: Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Read the terms at openstreetmap.org/copyright before reusing the names.

values.munis: List of the 78 municipality names, sorted alphabetically without accents. A row's municipality number is its position in this list, starting at 0.
values.kinds: List of the 19 type codes: municipio, town, village, barrio, neighborhood, road, route, hospital, school, university, civic, transport, park, beach, peak, water, landmark, airport, mall. A row's kind number is its position in this list, starting at 0.
values.items: List of rows [name, latitude, longitude, kind number, municipality number] with an optional note as a sixth value. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 7,506 rows carry a note.

data.gazetteer_kinds.plain: Each name in the place-name index has one of 19 types, such as municipality, street, highway number, hospital or beach. The type sets how the name is ranked and labeled in search results.
data.gazetteer_kinds.plain_es: Cada nombre del índice de lugares tiene uno de 19 tipos, como municipio, calle, número de carretera, hospital o playa. El tipo decide en qué orden aparece el nombre en los resultados de búsqueda y cómo se rotula.
data.gazetteer_kinds.definition: The kind is a number in each row of the index: its position in the 'kinds' list. The observatory's pages show a plain label for it in search results and rank some types ahead of others (a municipality ahead of a street).
data.gazetteer_kinds.method: gazetteer.py assigns the type from OpenStreetMap tags. For a named point it tests place, amenity, natural, historic, aeroway, leisure and shop, in that order. For a named area that is not a road it tests amenity, leisure, natural, aeroway, shop and historic. Roads are ways with a highway tag and a name or a PR route number. The first match wins. Place tags are read from points only. Only OpenStreetMap points and ways are read; the municipality and barrio rows come from Census Bureau boundaries (TIGERweb generalized, 500k, shoreline-clipped).
data.gazetteer_kinds.how_to_read: The counts show what OpenStreetMap volunteers have named. A low count can mean that few features exist or that few are mapped with a name. For example, the 2026-10 snapshot has 32 airport rows.
caveats: The types follow OpenStreetMap tags, not official categories. A clinic is filed under 'hospital'; a marina, a bay and an island mapped as a point are filed under 'water'.
Tourism listings (restaurants, hotels, attractions) are not part of this index.
The 'barrio' rows come from Census boundaries, not from OpenStreetMap.

values.municipio: Municipality. 78 rows, one per municipality. The point is the location of the OpenStreetMap town or city of the same name when it lies inside the boundary, otherwise a point inside the boundary. Search shows it as 'Municipality'.
values.town: Town or city: a point tagged place=town or place=city, except towns named like a municipality (those are the municipality rows). In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2 rows. Search shows it as 'Town'.
values.village: Small community: a point tagged place=village or place=hamlet. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 3,102 rows, all tagged hamlet. The note holds the OpenStreetMap place type. Search shows it as 'Community'.
values.barrio: Barrio (a division of a municipality): the barrio boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGERweb county subdivisions; 901 in the 2026-10 snapshot), written as 'Barrio' followed by the name and placed at a point inside the boundary. The note holds the barrio name alone. Search shows it as 'Barrio'.
values.neighborhood: Neighborhood: a point tagged place=suburb, neighbourhood, quarter or locality. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2,277 rows. The note holds the place type. Search shows it as 'Neighborhood'.
values.road: Named street: a way with a name and highway=motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, unclassified, residential, living_street or pedestrian. One row for each name and each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of the name's pieces; names whose pieces total less than 60 m are dropped. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 34,781 rows. Search shows it as 'Street'.
values.route: Highway number: Puerto Rico (PR) route numbers read from the ref tag, for example PR-52. One row for each number and each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of its pieces. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,679 rows, of which 1,224 carry a note with the road's local name. Search shows it as 'Highway'.
values.hospital: Hospital or clinic: amenity=hospital or clinic. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 372 rows. Search shows it as 'Hospital'.
values.school: School: amenity=school. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,679 rows. Search shows it as 'School'.
values.university: College or university: amenity=college or university. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 99 rows. Search shows it as 'College'.
values.civic: Public building: amenity=townhall, courthouse, police, fire_station, library, community_centre or post_office. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 704 rows. Search shows it as 'Public building'.
values.transport: Terminal: amenity=bus_station or ferry_terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 82 rows. Search shows it as 'Terminal'.
values.park: Park or sports ground: leisure=park, stadium, nature_reserve, sports_centre or golf_course. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,451 rows. Search shows it as 'Park'.
values.beach: Beach: natural=beach. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 195 rows. Search shows it as 'Beach'.
values.peak: Mountain: natural=peak or volcano. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 308 rows. Search shows it as 'Mountain'.
values.water: Water feature: leisure=marina, natural=bay or cape, or a point tagged place=island or islet. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 172 rows. Search shows it as 'Water'.
values.landmark: Landmark: amenity=theatre or arts_centre, natural=cave_entrance, or historic=castle, fort, monument, memorial, ruins, lighthouse, archaeological_site, building or church. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 470 rows. Search shows it as 'Landmark'.
values.airport: Airport: aeroway=aerodrome or terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 32 rows. Search shows it as 'Airport'.
values.mall: Shopping center: shop=mall or amenity=marketplace. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 66 rows. Search shows it as 'Shopping center'.

data.gazetteer_kinds.geography: Puerto Rico: 78 municipalities, with places on Vieques, Culebra and Mona Island
data.gazetteer_kinds.source_detail: gazetteer.py (KINDS, PLACE_KIND, AMENITY, LEISURE, NATURAL, HISTORIC, ROAD_CLASSES); labels from site/js/plan.js (KIND_INFO); municipality boundaries from US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K) and barrio boundaries from TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K), both shoreline-clipped (municipios.geojson, barrios.geojson)

layers.search_box.plain: The search box at the top finds municipalities, barrios, towns, streets, Puerto Rico (PR) highway numbers, landmarks, transit stops and routes, and tourism places. What you type is matched in your browser, except when you choose the online address lookup.
layers.search_box.plain_es: El buscador de la parte superior encuentra municipios, barrios, pueblos, calles, números de carreteras de Puerto Rico (PR), lugares emblemáticos, paradas y rutas de transporte colectivo, y lugares turísticos. Lo que se escribe se busca en el navegador, excepto cuando se elige la búsqueda de direcciones en línea.
layers.search_box.definition: Press / to jump to the box. Results start after 2 characters, and up to 12 are listed, each with an icon, a label and a line of detail. The arrow keys move through the list, Enter picks the first or the focused result, and Escape closes it. Two decimal numbers such as 18.4655, -66.1057 are read as coordinates. After 4 characters the list ends with 'Look up ... as an address online'. A pick flies the map there and drops a pin whose popup has 'Route from here' and 'Route to here'. What the box searches and what a pick does are listed below.
layers.search_box.method: plan.js (parseQuery, textScore, Gaz, attachSearch, searchEverything), shared by the 2D and 3D pages. Names are compared without accents or capitals. The online lookup asks nominatim.openstreetmap.org for up to 6 results inside a box around Puerto Rico (countrycodes=pr, bounded) and shows the first two parts of each address.
layers.search_box.how_to_read: Type part of a name. If a street has several matches, add the municipality.
caveats: The online address lookup sends the text you typed to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service, which has its own usage policy. It runs only when you pick that line. Nothing else you type leaves the page.
A misspelling finds nothing. Matching is on letters, after accents and capitals are removed.

The 2D tourism results follow your category, confidence and worship filters, so a place can be missing because a filter hides it. They appear only once the tourism place listings are loaded: until then the last line of the results offers to load them (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10).

values.Places and areas: Municipalities and the place-name index. The index holds towns, communities, barrios, neighborhoods, PR highways, named streets, hospitals, schools, colleges, public buildings, terminals, parks, beaches, mountains, water, landmarks, airports and shopping centers.
values.Tourism places: Searched by name or type. On the 2D map the box follows the current category, confidence and worship filters. In the 3D view it follows the category buttons, confidence 0.50 and no places of worship.
values.Transit: Scheduled stops, stations, terminals and airports by name. The header box also searches transit routes by number, name or operator. The planner's boxes search the same list without routes.
values.A pick on the 2D map: A municipality opens its profile, a tourism place opens its card, a stop opens its card and a route fits on the screen.
values.A pick in the 3D view: The camera flies to the result, or fits the municipality or route, and a pin card opens.

view.label: 2D map: search box
3D view: search box

layers.csv_downloads.plain: Six buttons on the map and Housing pages save data as files: a municipality table, the places of a municipality, two economy tables, a housing table and a planned route. These files are made in your browser. The data dictionary page adds two more download buttons and a download link for each published data file.
layers.csv_downloads.plain_es: Seis botones en las páginas del mapa y de Vivienda guardan datos como archivos: una tabla de municipios, los lugares de un municipio, dos tablas económicas, una tabla de vivienda y una ruta planificada. Estos archivos se crean en el navegador. La página del diccionario de datos agrega dos botones de descarga más y un enlace de descarga para cada archivo de datos publicado.
layers.csv_downloads.definition: All comma-separated values (CSV) files are UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so that Excel shows accents correctly. Cells are separated by commas, and text that holds a comma, a quote or a line break is put in quotes. A text cell that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe, so that a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula. Empty cells mean no value. The buttons are listed below with the file each one saves.
layers.csv_downloads.method: app.js (downloadCsv), economy.js (ecSaveCsv), housing.js (saveCsv) and plan.js (download). On the dictionary page, dictionary.js (downloadSeries, downloadDictionary, saveCsv) does the same. Files are built in the browser and nothing is uploaded.
layers.csv_downloads.how_to_read: Cite the stored values in the files, not the rounded numbers on screen. Add the snapshot label and the date you downloaded them. A file has no citation of its own. Use the Cite button on the dictionary entries of the datasets it holds.
caveats: The files carry the licenses of their sources. Check each source's terms before you reuse or publish a file.
The places file can include helper columns whose names start with an underscore. They are search aids and can be ignored.
A file records what the page held when you pressed the button. Filters and settings on screen change what a places or table file holds.

values.Download municipality table (CSV): Rankings tab. File pr_digital_twin_municipalities_<snapshot label>.csv, for example pr_digital_twin_municipalities_Snapshot_2026-10.csv. One row for each of the 78 municipalities with every field of municipalities.json. Nested fields (places by category, land use in km²) become columns named with their parent. In Snapshot 2026-10 eight shares of places are blank for the 14 municipalities with no stop counted: transit_pct, acc_cur400_pct, acc_cur800_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct, acc_sun400_pct, acc_hub400_pct and acc_paper_pct. The other access fields (the stop counts by state, access_n and access_as_of) are included.
values.Download <municipality> places (CSV): Municipality tab. File <municipality>_places.csv. The button loads the place listings first when they are not loaded yet (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10). One row for each place the map is showing in that municipality, so it follows the category buttons, the confidence slider and the worship switch. Columns are the fields of places.json and, when the access file has loaded, ts_m, ts_calls and ts_we of place_access.json. A column named id is never exported, and neither are socials, phone or email.
values.Download CSV (workbench table): Economy workbench, Table tab. File pr_economy_layers.csv. GEOID (the geographic identifier code of the Census Bureau), Municipality and one column for each visible layer, for the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico.
values.Download all years (CSV): Economy dataset dialog. File pr_economy_<dataset>.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when the source publishes margins. Values as published.
values.Download CSV (Full data): Housing page, in a dataset's 'Full data' dialog. File pr_housing_<name>.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when published. Published tables give their own rows. The Puerto Rico row has GEOID 72.
values.GeoJSON (route planner): Route planner. File planned_route.geojson. This is a GeoJSON file, not a CSV: the route line with a few results and one point for each chosen place.
values.Download all years (CSV), dictionary pag: Data dictionary page, on the entries that describe a yearly series (a field of economy_series.json or housing_series.json). File pr_digital_twin_<id>.csv, with each dot of the id turned into an underscore, for example pr_digital_twin_economy_qcew_jobs.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when the source publishes margins. Values as published. The file has 79 rows: the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (GEOID 72).
values.Download the dictionary (CSV): Data dictionary page. File pr_digital_twin_data_dictionary.csv. One row for each entry, whatever the filters on the page, with these columns: id, name, area, group, kind, type, unit, geography, years, updates, plain description, definition, how it is computed, how to read it, cautions, sources, source detail, data fields, related entries and the date added.
values.Data file links, dictionary page: The data file names under 'Where it appears' on an entry and in the table of published data files are download links to the files themselves, as published in the data folder. These files are not made in your browser.

view.label: 2D map: Rankings tab
Housing page: Data catalog
Data dictionary page: download buttons

measures.route_export.plain: The GeoJSON button saves the planned route as planned_route.geojson. The file holds the line, the points you chose and six of the results shown.
measures.route_export.plain_es: El botón "GeoJSON" guarda la ruta planificada como planned_route.geojson. El archivo tiene la línea, los puntos escogidos y seis de los resultados que se muestran.
measures.route_export.definition: A GeoJSON file (a standard text format for map shapes) with one line feature (the route) and one point feature for each chosen point. The line has the properties name, created, source, follows_roads, length_km, stops, residents_within_400m, tourism_places_within_400m, share_parallel_to_existing_routes_pct, share_in_flood_hazard_area_pct and municipalities. Each point has name, order and role.
measures.route_export.method: plan.js builds the file from the current result. Coordinates are longitude and latitude (World Geodetic System 1984, WGS 84). A line that follows roads has 5 decimals; points have 6.
measures.route_export.how_to_read: Open the file in a mapping program to keep or share a plan. The numbers are those shown when you pressed the button.
caveats: Not in the file: the running time, residents with no scheduled stop, lodgings, the protected-area share and the connections.
'created' is the date in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time), so it can be one day ahead of the date in Puerto Rico in the evening.
A number that had not finished loading when you pressed the button is left out of the file.
The file carries the data licenses of its inputs (OpenStreetMap roads, Overture places, FEMA, Census and timetable feeds). Check the terms of each before you publish it.
The file holds the points you chose to 6 decimals (about 0.1 m) with their labels. If you chose a home address, the file shows it. Remove it before you share the file.

values.name: 'Planned route' for the line; the place label for a point.
values.created: Date the file was made, as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.
values.follows_roads: true when Follow roads is on and every leg follows roads; false otherwise.
values.length_km: Route length in km with two decimals (the number in the 'Route length' entry).
values.stops: Labels of the chosen points joined with ' > '.
values.residents_within_400m: Residents within 400 m of the route.
values.tourism_places_within_400m: Tourism places within 400 m of the route.
values.share_parallel_to_existing_routes_pct: Share of the route within 150 m of an existing route (percent).
values.share_in_flood_hazard_area_pct: Share of the route in a flood hazard area (percent).
values.municipalities: Names of the municipalities crossed, joined with ', '.
values.order: Position of the point along the route, from 1.
values.role: 'from' for the first point, 'to' for the last, 'stop' for points between.

measures.route_export.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

layers.share_link_2d.plain: The 2D map keeps its view in the part of the page address after the # sign: municipality, position, layers that are on, shading, planned route and economy layers. Copy the address to share the view.
layers.share_link_2d.plain_es: El mapa 2D guarda su vista en la parte de la dirección de la página que va después del signo #: municipio, posición, capas activadas, sombreado, ruta planificada y capas económicas. Copie la dirección para compartir la vista.
layers.share_link_2d.definition: The address is rewritten about a quarter of a second after each change, without adding steps to the browser's back button. Its form is #<Municipality>&c=<lat>,<lng>,<zoom>&l=<layers>&s=<shading>&r=<route>&e=<economy>&ey=<year>&eb=<base>&slr=<feet>. Parts that do not apply are left out, except c and l, which are always written. The parts are listed below. When the address changes while the page is open, the municipality, position, layers, shading and sea level are applied again. The route (r) and the economy parts (e, ey, eb) are read only when the page loads. To use a changed one, reload the page. The page's title carries the municipality name. The '3D + Time' link in the header carries the position (c) and the route (r) to the 3D view.
layers.share_link_2d.method: app.js (writeHash, parseHash, applyHash, LAYER_KEYS), network.js and economy.js.
layers.share_link_2d.how_to_read: Open the link in a new tab to check it before you share it. A hand-made link must list every layer you want on. Example: index.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,12&l=muni,flood&s=sfha_pct shows the flood zones and shades the municipalities by the share of places in a flood hazard area, with no pins.
caveats: Layer settings other than those listed, such as the category buttons, the confidence slider, the worship switch and the open tab, are not kept in the address.
A link records choices, not data. If the observatory's data change after a new snapshot, the same link can show different numbers.

The r= part holds the exact coordinates of every point of a planned route, to about 11 meters. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

values.#<Municipality>: A municipality name, URL-encoded, such as #San%20Juan. It is matched ignoring accents and capitals. An unknown name gives a message. A link with a municipality opens the Municipality tab.
values.c: c=<latitude>,<longitude>,<zoom>: the map center (4 decimals) and the zoom level, a whole number on the 2D map's scale. When c is present the map does not fly to the municipality.
values.l: l=<layers>: the layers that are ON, separated by commas. The list is complete: a layer that is not named is switched off, including tourism places (places) and boundaries (muni). A link with l=flood therefore shows no pins and no boundaries.
values.l=taxi: Taxi stands and electric vehicle charging.
values.s: s=<field>: a measure of the retired 'Shade municipalities by' menu, for example s=sfha_pct. Old links keep working: the measure opens as its dataset (app.js SHADE_DS) and the address is rewritten with e=.
values.slr: slr=<feet>: the sea level slider, a whole number from 1 to 10. It is written only when the sea level layer is on.
values.r: r=<lat>,<lng>;<lat>,<lng>...: the points of a planned route, 4 decimals, from 2 to 8 points. The link opens the Transit tab and plans the route.
values.e, ey, eb: The Analysis tab's layers, year and base year. See the entry on Economy links.

view.label: 2D map: flood zones, shaded by flood exposure
2D map: a municipality

layers.share_link_3d.plain: The 3D view reads two items from the page address: the camera center and zoom (c) and a planned route (r). Layers and clocks are not kept in the address.
layers.share_link_3d.plain_es: La vista 3D lee dos datos de la dirección de la página: el centro y el acercamiento de la cámara (c) y una ruta planificada (r). Las capas y los relojes no se guardan en la dirección.
layers.share_link_3d.definition: The form is 3d.html#c=<lat>,<lng>,<zoom>&r=<lat>,<lng>;<lat>,<lng>. The zoom number is on the 2D map's scale: the 3D view subtracts 1 when it opens the link and adds 1 when it writes one. The 3D page writes the address when it opens and again whenever the route changes. It does not follow the camera as you move. The 'Map' link in the header carries the camera and route to the 2D map. An address with r= opens the Route tab and plans the route.
layers.share_link_3d.how_to_read: Open the link to check it. Tilt and rotation are not in the link, so the camera opens at the page's usual angle. Example: 3d.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,14 opens near the center of San Juan.
caveats: The tilt, rotation, open tab, switches and the clock settings are not saved in the address.

The r= part holds the exact coordinates of every point of a planned route, to about 11 meters. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

view.label: 3D view: San Juan

layers.share_link_economy.plain: The Analysis tab writes its layers, year and base year into the page address. The 'Copy link' button copies the address, and opening it brings the same layers back.
layers.share_link_economy.plain_es: La pestaña Análisis escribe sus capas, el año y el año base en la dirección de la página. El botón "Copiar enlace" copia la dirección, y al abrirla vuelven las mismas capas.
layers.share_link_economy.definition: The part e= holds the layers, in list order, separated by commas (written %2C in the address). Each layer is ten items joined by dots: <dataset>.<mode>.<show-as>.<ramp>.<classes>.<visible>.<fixed>.<inflation>.<opacity>.<color>. For example poverty_pct.f.value.blue.q.1.1.0.85.0 is a shaded poverty rate, as published, in blue, with equal-count classes, visible, the same classes in every year, not inflation-adjusted, at 85% opacity. A link with an e= part opens the Analysis tab. These parts are read only when the page loads. If you change them in a page that is already open, reload it. To keep other map layers out of the way, add l=muni (see the 2D link entry). The first two shaded layers form the bivariate map.
layers.share_link_economy.method: economy.js (ecEncode, ecRestore, ECON.extra). The button 'Copy link' (ecCopy) writes the address and copies it. If your browser blocks the copy, a message asks you to copy the address from the address bar.
layers.share_link_economy.how_to_read: Build a link by copying one from the page and changing the year, rather than writing the layer codes by hand.
caveats: Settings of the workbench (open tab, chosen places) are not kept in the address.
A link names datasets by key. If a dataset is renamed or removed in a later version, its layer is dropped.

values.<dataset>: The dataset key, for example poverty_pct or qcew_jobs. Unknown keys are ignored.
values.<mode>: f for a shaded layer, s for symbols.
values.<show-as>: One of the 'Show as' codes: value, per1000, perkm2, sharePR, shareJobs, lq, perCapita, index, diff, change, pctile. A code that the dataset does not offer becomes value.
values.<ramp>: blue, green, gold, red or gray.
values.<classes>: q for quantiles, e for equal intervals, j for natural breaks.
values.<fixed>: 1 for 'Same classes in every year', 0 for off.
values.<colour>: A number 0 to 4 for the symbol color: 0 Red, 1 Blue, 2 Gold, 3 Green, 4 Charcoal.
values.ey: ey=<year>: the year. Left out when the year control is on 'Latest'.
values.eb: eb=<year>: the base year of 'Change measured from'. Left out when it is 2014.

view.label: 2D map: poverty rate in 2022 as a shaded layer

layers.share_link_housing.plain: The Housing page keeps the municipality, the data year, the base year and an open dataset in the page address, so you can share the exact view.
layers.share_link_housing.plain_es: La página de Vivienda guarda en la dirección de la página el municipio, el año de los datos, el año base y el conjunto de datos abierto, para poder compartir exactamente la misma vista.
layers.share_link_housing.definition: The form is housing.html?m=<municipality>&y=<year>&c=<base year>&d=<dataset>#<section>. The page updates the address when you pick a municipality, a year or a base year. It adds d when a 'Full data' dialog is open and removes it when the dialog closes. A link with d opens that dialog after the page has loaded. A link with an anchor scrolls to that section.
layers.share_link_housing.method: housing.js (writeUrl, openDataset, init). The page reads the address once, when it loads.
layers.share_link_housing.how_to_read: Use d to point a reader at one dataset's full table, and y to fix the year. Example: housing.html?m=Ponce&y=2020&c=2014&d=median_gross_rent#profile opens the profile of Ponce for 2020, with changes measured from 2014, and the full table of median gross rent.
caveats: The page does not check that y is in range. Years after the latest data show the latest available value with a note.
The id table2 is not a valid d value. Use population for the population table.

values.m: m=<municipality>: the municipality of the profile. Matched ignoring accents and capitals.
values.y: y=<year>: the data year (2010 to 2025 in Snapshot 2026-10). Left out for 'Latest'.
values.c: c=<year>: the base year of 'Change measured from' (2010 to 2023 in Snapshot 2026-10). Left out when it is 2012.
values.d: d=<dataset>: opens a dataset's 'Full data' dialog. A series key such as median_gross_rent, or one of the published-table ids table6, t6live, table7, table10, grapilive, smocapilive.
values.embed: ?embed: hides the header bar and the contents bar, for use inside another web page.

view.label: Housing page: Ponce, 2020, with the rent table open
